unknownEntries.subject: Synchronize ranged release timeline and payload
unknownEntries.body:
Add deterministic ranged wind-up/release synchronization by introducing `AttackTiming` and a networked `RangedAttackRelease` snapshot that captures committed projectile data at acceptance and consumes it at the authoritative release tick. `PlayerCombatNetworkController` now advances/cancels pending releases independently of input, preserves cooldown behavior, supports migration-safe restore, and exposes release-aware attack events.

Update ranged presentation to follow the confirmed release timeline (animator + VFX), add per-weapon ranged release timing and VFX lead configuration, harden ranged/projectile validation paths, and expand edit/play mode tests plus architecture docs to cover release scheduling, cancellation, restore behavior, and calibration.

unknownEntries.body:
Implements changes from the PvE audit (US-49) to finalize the Dungeon pressure systems.

- Replaced obsolete EnemyCollapseDespawner and queue with explicit Collapse validation logic in DungeonPressureConfig.
- Updated EnemyReinforcementDirector to generate reinforcements during Collapse, using ActiveAvatarObjects to ensure minimum spawn distances.
- Added disableLoot support to NetworkSpawnManager, allowing Collapse reinforcements to spawn without loot tables to prevent exploitable rewards.
- Set authoritative DefaultDungeonPressureConfig durations (15m Normal, 5m Early, 2m Critical) with a provisional 2m Collapse policy.
- Updated DungeonPressureArchitecture.md to reflect the active components and runner-scoped lifecycle of the pressure controller.

Tests:
- Updated DungeonPressureConfigTests to cover new validation rules.

unknownEntries.subject: Split player spawns into team-based areas
unknownEntries.body: Refactors scene spawn configuration to move players out of generic SpawnGroupDefinition into dedicated PlayerSpawnAreaDefinition collections, and marks SpawnGroupType.Players as unsupported in initial world-group dispatch. NetworkSpawnManager now tracks player areas separately, validates them against scene ownership, uses fresh-session-only preflight checks, and resolves player spawn transforms via team/participant assignment rules. RaidParticipantSpawnRules was expanded to validate full fresh launch context, enforce unique transform/position usage, and deterministically map participants to area/point pairs by team appearance and intra-team order. Updated gameplay scene data, architecture docs, and edit-mode tests to cover the new model and reject legacy generic player groups.

unknownEntries.subject: Unify the Stash screen with the Raid inventory and prepare Equipment in Town
unknownEntries.body:
The Stash screen was a fork of the Raid inventory that stopped matching it when
the Raid UI moved into the prefab: it still instantiated slots at runtime, kept
two dead RaidLootPanelView components wired to a removed _slotPrefab field, and
floated its two prepared weapon slots over the loadout panel with hardcoded
anchored positions. Town preparation also covered weapons only, so the armor
introduced by the six-slot Equipment work could not be prepared before a raid.

Stash screen composition
- LobbyStashUI stops creating UI. It binds two authored RaidLootPanelView panels,
  six authored RaidInventorySlotView Equipment views, both bulk buttons and the
  context menu, and pads each received stack list with empty entries up to its
  authored pool exactly as RaidInventoryProjection does for the Raid screen.
  Content beyond the pool is reported once and the panel shows its existing
  "Lleno" feedback instead of silently dropping stacks.
- Both panels are TransferWithContextMenu, so a stack can be equipped from the
  Stash or from the Loadout. The menu offers only the slots EquipmentSlotRules
  reports as compatible, resolved from the category now carried by
  RaidInventorySlotData, so the view needs no catalog of its own. A left click on
  an occupied Equipment slot releases that exact slot.
- TownStashView becomes an authored component that only shows and hides the
  screen; TownStashPresenter resolves it instead of adding components and the
  Canvas sorting order is authored in the prefab. The development-only [StashUI]
  traces are gone; the dependency warnings stay.
- StashInventory.prefab now holds the panels, both 16-slot pools, the equipment
  panel and the screen root. The prefab is the only source of truth for that
  layout: the temporary authoring tools that seeded both inventory screens are
  removed, so nothing can regenerate the hierarchy, renumber the authored slots
  or overwrite manual layout work. Adding a slot means adding it in the prefab
  and appending it to the panel's _authoredSlots.

Town Equipment preparation
- PreparedWeaponLoadout becomes PreparedEquipmentLoadout, covering the six slots
  of EquipmentSlot. EquipmentSlotRules owns the canonical slot order and decides
  compatibility; weapon slots additionally require a usable WeaponDefinition, and
  one identity used by several slots requires one owned unit per reference.
- LocalProfileStore exposes TryAssignPreparedEquipment/TryClearPreparedEquipment.
  Prepared units must belong to the Loadout because that is what the reservation
  transfers, so equipping a unit that still lives in the Stash pulls the missing
  units into the Loadout inside the same atomic commit; a rejected assignment
  moves nothing and a full Loadout rejects the pull. Releasing a slot leaves the
  unit in the Loadout. Reconciliation releases the last slots first.
- The recovery weapon guarantee and the Slot 2 to Slot 1 normalization no longer
  overwrite prepared armor: armor is optional, never granted and never rewritten.
- The profile codec gains four additive armor fields for the profile and for the
  reservation. CurrentSchemaVersion stays 1 on purpose: the fields are optional,
  so a profile saved before them decodes with empty armor, while bumping the
  version would reject every existing local profile as UnsupportedVersion.
- RaidAdmissionData carries one reference per Equipment slot in
  EquipmentSlotRules.AllSlots order, RaidLoadoutRules validates range, the
  mandatory weapon and reference multiplicity, and the admission token moves to
  canonical version 6 with four extra bytes, still inside its 512-byte bound.
- TryInitializePreparedEquipment equips the six slots on spawn and rechecks slot
  compatibility against the catalog before extracting any unit, so a reference
  that no longer fits its slot rejects the admission instead of dropping the
  piece. FusionSessionLauncher verifies all six slots before confirming.

Design alignment
04 - Character Build Design puts armor inside the prepared build and allows
changing it in Town, and keeps one valid weapon as the only launch requirement.

unknownEntries.subject: Complete two-slot weapon equipment and expedition preparation
unknownEntries.body:
Extend Weapon Equipment to two authoritative quick slots and carry them across the
Town-Raid boundary. Prepared Weapon Slot 1 and Slot 2 are non-owning references over units
that remain in the Town Loadout; they enter the raid inside PendingLoadoutReservation, travel
as compact one-based references into ReservedLoadout in the version 5 admission token, and are
materialized by State Authority into replicated Equipment without duplicating inventory
ownership. Add the Town assignment UI over the Loadout context menu, raid inventory weapon
slots, weapon selection input, and the corresponding persistence, codec and admission coverage.

Introduce an expedition preparation boundary that runs before the reservation so requiring a
valid equipped weapon can no longer make Start Raid inert. TryPrepareExpeditionWeapons is
atomic, deterministic and idempotent: it leaves a valid Slot 1 untouched, normalizes the
effective selection when only Slot 2 is occupied, grants exactly one configured recovery weapon
when nothing is prepared while reusing an owned unit first, and fails explicitly on a persisted
reference that no longer resolves instead of overwriting it. Add the recovery_sword definition
with its own weapon definition, excluded from loot tables and without economic value, and
configure it as the Town recovery policy. TryCreateLoadoutReservation keeps requiring a valid
prepared weapon as a domain invariant, and Raid never grants recovery.

Stop a rejected local preparation from deadlocking the shared Town preparation.
TryStoreRaidLaunchContext now returns RaidLaunchPreparationResult so a transient retry is
distinguishable from a permanent rejection; a peer that cannot prepare reports it once per
launch revision instead of sending a false acknowledgement or waiting silently, and the State
Authority remains the only canceller. Arm a deadline for the acknowledgement phase so a launch
revision cannot wait indefinitely for a missing acknowledgement, and surface the rejection
reason through the existing Town feedback channel.

Fix two crashes in the new equipment surface. Every read-only query is guarded behind the
spawn check so presentation components that run their lifecycle callbacks during prefab
instantiation report no equipment rather than throwing on networked state, and the equipment
request RPC validates its byte-backed kind by range because Enum.IsDefined rejects the boxed
int outright.

commits.subject: feat(combat): sync melee impacts with contact, add hitstop and hit reaction
commits.body:
Melee damage resolved during the wind-up, before the weapon visually
reached the target. Each melee weapon now releases at its own measured
contact, and confirmed melee hits get an attacker-local hitstop and a
directional target reaction. Presentation only: no new networked state,
gameplay timing, damage, knockback or movement changes beyond the
release calibration.

Release calibration (AttackReleaseSeconds; VFX StartSeconds unchanged,
ReleaseLeadSeconds = release - start keeps each VFX clip moment):
- Arming Sword 0.10 -> 0.265, Magic Sword 0.25 -> 0.48
- Long Sword 0.08 -> 0.35, Zweihander 0.25 -> 0.50
- Great Hammer 0.26 -> 0.55, Rapier 0.19 -> 0.35
- Rondel Dagger / Magic Cinquedea 0.14 -> 0.30, Spellbook 0.625 -> 0.65
- Off Hand VFX uses the Main presenter boundary tolerance so a non-zero
  lead cannot start it one frame late.

Hitstop:
- Melee confirmations are tagged with hand slot, attack sequence and
  weapon inside the synchronous melee Execute scope and carried by the
  existing State Authority -> Input Authority feedback RPC; ranged,
  abilities and zero/rejected damage stay untagged.
- AttackHitstop maps only the presentation seconds of each hand/legacy
  timeline (Main, Off and VFX freeze together); acceptance and
  cancellation keep raw render time. One pause per attack sequence, late
  confirmations spend the budget and never rewind.
- HitstopTargetFreeze pauses the target's Animators locally and restores
  them on expiry, death, Downed, equipment change or despawn.
- WeaponDefinition.Presentation.HitstopSeconds: daggers 0.04, Rapier and
  Spellbook 0.05, one-handed swords 0.06, Long Sword 0.08, Zweihander
  0.10, Great Hammer 0.12; ranged 0.

Hit reaction:
- Feedback RPC also carries the hit direction.
- MeleeHitReactionProfile assets (Light/Medium/Heavy) referenced by
  WeaponDefinition.Presentation.HitReaction.
- HitReactionPlayback applies flash, axis-aligned squash snapped to
  1/16 and a 16 PPU pixel-snapped nudge; the peak holds for the hitstop
  pause, then recovers and restores captured base values exactly.
- DamageFeedbackPresenter.TryPlayMeleeReaction coalesces the matching
  Health-drop pulse, guards rapid retriggers and keeps the generic
  feedback for every other damage source and peer.

Tests: MeleeReleaseCalibrationTests (contact table),
SwordSlashPresentationTests (measured Main/Off contact),
CanonicalSlashGeneratorTests, AttackHitstopTests, WeaponHitstopTests,
HitstopTargetFreezeTests, MeleeHitReactionProfileTests,
HitReactionPlaybackTests, DamageFeedbackPresenterTests,
PlayerCombatNetworkControllerPlayModeTests (melee tags and direction).

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md release contract, Melee hitstop and
Melee hit reaction sections.

Player-Improved: Melee weapons now deal damage when the blade visibly connects, with a short impact pause and a hit reaction that feels heavier for bigger weapons.

commits.subject: fix(networking): consume raid reservations by participation outcome
commits.body:
Raid admission now marks the backend reservation as admitted instead of
deleting it, so the host can publish the extraction result and the
next raid starts from the real Town Inventory and Equipment.

Outcome wiring:
- Admission confirmation calls the admit endpoint.
- Leaving a raid without a local extraction receipt for that raid
  (return, defeat, abandon, closure, definitive disconnect, failed Host
  Migration, discarded reconnect ticket) clears the reservation once as
  a loss. Reconnectable Client disconnects keep it.
- Recovery after admission never rolls the reservation back.
- Login: an admitted orphan with no pending extraction commit is
  discarded locally without restoring items and cleared as a loss; a
  non-admitted orphan keeps the rollback; a pending extraction commit
  keeps its retry. A local recovery failure is logged and login
  continues, as before.
- 409 EXTRACTION_RESULT_PENDING is only logged.

Tests:
- RaidReservationLifecycleTests: admitted orphan loss, non-admitted
  rollback, pending extraction preserved, rejections leave state
  unchanged.

Docs: LocalPlayerPersistence (backend reservation lifetime),
Extraction and RemoteIdentityAndAuth reservation requirement.

Refs: odd/tasks/raid-reservation-lifecycle.md T2, T3
Player-Fixed: Gear equipped in Town now comes with you into the raid, and extracting keeps your loot.

commits.subject: fix(backend): keep raid reservations alive until the raid outcome
commits.body:
Admission now marks the pending reservation as admitted instead of
deleting it, so a player-hosted extraction publish finds the active
reservation that bounded host trust requires (63f574df6). Before, the
client cleared the reservation at admission, every extraction publish
failed with NO_ACTIVE_RESERVATION, the commit failed with
NO_AUTHORITATIVE_RESULT and the backend Loadout stayed empty for the
next raid.

Contract:
- POST /character/me/inventory/reservation/admit { reservationId }
  sets admittedAt once; same id is idempotent; missing or different
  reservation returns 422 NO_ACTIVE_RESERVATION.
- Reservations serialize admittedAt (ISO string or null).
- Rollback of an admitted reservation returns 409 RESERVATION_ADMITTED.
- A loss clear (DELETE without rollback) or a replacement of an
  admitted reservation returns 409 EXTRACTION_RESULT_PENDING while an
  unconsumed authoritative result targets the account; otherwise the
  reserved items are consumed without being returned.
- A new launch never restores the items of an admitted reservation.

Tests:
- inventory.lifecycle.test.js: admission, validation, revision guards,
  loss, rollback rejection, unchanged state on rejection.
- raid.result / extraction.commit: publish and commit with an admitted
  reservation.
- admission.integration: reserve, admit, publish, guarded clear,
  commit round trip on MongoDB.

Refs: odd/tasks/raid-reservation-lifecycle.md T1

commits.subject: feat(combat): resolve projectile contacts by declared impact contract
commits.body:
NetworkProjectile now resolves every contact of its tick sweep in
authoritative spatial order instead of keeping only the nearest hit
(Doc 18 section 5, TASK-249). Contacts are classified as orb
interceptor, target or blocker, ordered by distance with a
deterministic tie-break, deduplicated per subject per event and
discarded after the terminating contact.

Each projectile prefab declares a re-impact policy (once per target,
once per continuous contact, periodic pulses), a maximum impact count
and a pulse interval. Defaults (once per target, 1 impact) keep the
previous first-contact behavior for every existing prefab. Re-impact
progress (impact count, next pulse tick, 8-entry ledger) is networked
flight state. An invalid contract logs an error and the projectile
despawns without impacts.

An already-consumed orb is now passed through and no longer lets the
projectile skip a wall or target behind it in the same tick.

Tests:
- ProjectileContactResolverTests: Doc 18 T15, T16, T17, each policy,
  impact-count termination, blockers, tie-break, settings validation.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture section 6, AbilitySystemArchitecture
Arcane flight.

commits.subject: feat(combat): align the combat action cycle with Game Design 17
commits.body:
Sprint, Weapon Set switching, Crossbow reload and action exclusivity
now follow Game Design 17 sections 4-7 and 9 (TASK-248).

Sprint and attacks:
- PlayerCombatNetworkController.IsOffensiveStartRequested reports a
  weapon start the active set can accept this tick, from replicated
  state only. Movement (-10) ends Sprint on that tick, before combat
  accepts the attack, so it moves at walking speed and spends no
  sprint Stamina.
- Sprint stays suppressed during the Execution Window and any pending
  release, and resumes automatically if still held.

Crossbow load state (GD 09 section 13):
- WeaponDefinition gains UsesReload and ReloadSeconds (Reload Time),
  separate from AttackIntervalSeconds (Shot Interval).
- WeaponHandAttackState carries a tick-only WeaponReloadState. A
  committed shot unloads the hand; the authority reloads it once the
  release resolves, while its set is active, not sprinting, alive,
  not Downed and combat is enabled. Any other tick discards partial
  progress, so Sprint, a set switch and Downed restart it from zero.
  An Unloaded hand is unavailable; a stowed Loaded weapon stays
  Loaded; reload costs no Stamina.
- Light Crossbow: provisional 1.3 s reload, so 0.3 s release plus
  reload keeps the 1.6 s baseline cycle. Pending Balance confirmation.
- Load identity is template-based until weapon instances exist.

Mutual exclusion (GD 17 section 7.3):
- Ability starts reject with the new AbilityActivationFailure
  .AttackInProgress (byte 11, appended) during a weapon Execution
  Window or pending release, before cooldown, payment or planning.
  HUD shows "Ataque en curso"; the sandbox describes it.
- Consumables also reject during the Execution Window.
- Weapon Set switching remains blocked only during the window, and
  full Stamina cost is still debited once at acceptance (TASK-222).

Tests:
- WeaponReloadStateTests (EditMode): deadline, interruption, stowed,
  zero and invalid timing, definition validation
- PlayerMovementRulesTests: held Sprint resumes after execution
- RaidAbilityHudModelTests: AttackInProgress mapping and notification
- PlayerEquipmentPlayModeTests: Sprint-to-attack tick, reload
  availability, Sprint and set-switch reload interruption
- PlayerAbilityRuntimeNetworkControllerPlayModeTests: ability and
  consumable rejection during a weapon attack

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture (combat action cycle),
PlayerMovementArchitecture section 20.1, AbilitySystemArchitecture.

Validation: affected EditMode suites 101/101; Equipment, Ability,
Combat and Downed PlayMode fixtures 103/106, with the 3 failures
reproducing identically without this change. Real Host/Client and
Host Migration remain unverified.

Refs: TASK-248
Player-Added: The crossbow now has to reload after each shot; sprinting or switching weapon sets interrupts the reload and it starts over.
Player-Improved: Attacking while sprinting now stops the sprint and attacks instantly, and sprint picks up again on its own if you keep holding it.
Player-Improved: Abilities can no longer be cast in the middle of a weapon attack; the HUD tells you an attack is in progress.

commits.subject: feat(combat): award PvP Last Hit and Assist credit per Downed cycle
commits.body:
Enemy players now produce PvP Experience through the Downed cycle
(GD 19 sections 4-6, 14; TASK-246). The victim's new
PlayerPvpCombatCreditNetworkController freezes one provisional Last Hit
and its Assists on Active -> Downed, confirms them once when that same
cycle ends in definitive Defeat (drain, reserve damage, absence or
collapse) and cancels them on revive. PlayerDownedStateNetworkController
notifies it synchronously through the new IDownedCycleObserver.

Attribution rules:
- Last Hit goes to the resolvable player source of the downing hit, only
  against an initial enemy; unresolved affiliation fails closed.
  Creatures and environment produce no credit.
- Hits on a Downed target, including the downing hit, never record
  contributions, so finishers cannot steal or open credit.
- Contributions stay window-based across cycles; only credits reset.
- Assist candidates are initial teammates of the Last Hit with effective
  in-window damage, effective Restoration support on the Last Hit or a
  damage contributor, or an empowered basic attack (credited to the
  Empower caster, PvP targets only; PvE assists unchanged).
- _maxAssistsPerTarget defaults to 1 (GD 05 section 19 table); 0 keeps
  every eligible teammate (GD 19 section 6.2). Pending design decision.
  With a limit, the latest contribution wins; ties go to the lowest
  RaidParticipantId.

Rewards: base PvP Experience 25 on NetworkPlayer.prefab, PvpKill at
base and PvpAssist at floor(base / 2) = 12, ledger-before-consumption
with a 1 s retry; non-Raiding recipients get no new XP.

Contracts to review:
- DamageRequest gains an optional EmpowerSourceId; melee and ranged
  basic attacks (RangedAttackRelease, FusionProjectileSpawner,
  NetworkProjectile) carry it; abilities never do.
- EmpowerNetworkEffect replicates its source participant.
- CombatContributionTracker stores the latest contribution kind per
  participant packed in one word, and now unregisters as an isolated
  capability so it never clears co-located collider mappings (fixes
  projectiles hitting their despawning caster).
- NetworkPlayer.prefab composes CombatContributionTracker and the
  credit controller; all new state is [Networked] with restore guards.

Tests:
- PvpCombatCreditPlayModeTests (34): T02-01..07, T03-01, 03-07, limit
  and tie-break, Empower, terminal sources, retry and state copy
- MeleeAttackTests, RangedAttackReleaseTests: Empower source forwarding
- KillExperiencePrefabTests: player composes the PvP producer

Docs: DownedAndReviveArchitecture section 11, ProgressionArchitecture.

Validation: full EditMode and PlayMode suites show no new failures
against a baseline without this change (23 EditMode and 38 PlayMode
failures reproduce identically). Real Host/Client and Host Migration
remain unverified.

Player-Added: Downing an enemy player now earns experience once they are finally defeated, and a teammate who helped earns assist experience; reviving the enemy cancels both.

commits.subject: fix(presentation): drain render event queues without subscribers
commits.body:
Render drains used `Event?.Invoke(queue.Dequeue())`. With no
subscriber, the null-conditional call skips evaluating its argument,
so the item was never dequeued. A `while` drain then spun forever on
the main thread and froze the Unity Editor. A pickup grant received
by a local Input Authority without a bound loot HUD reproduced it
(UtilityExpeditionPlayModeTests.UtilityCooldown_PersistsAcrossDropAndPickup).

Dequeue into a local before invoking in every affected drain:
- PlayerLootReceiver (LootGranted)
- PlayerWeaponEquipmentNetworkController (EquipRequestResolved)
- PlayerCombatNetworkController (CombatFeedbackResolved)
- TownPartyDirectory (InvitationResultReceived)
- PlayerInteractionNetworkController (InteractionResolved): its bounded
  loop did not hang but left events queued for later subscribers

Tests:
- NetworkLootPickupPartialPickupPlayModeTests.
  PickupGrant_WithoutPresentationSubscriber_DrainsOnRender

Validation: the previously hanging test passes; pickup fixture 6/6 and
PlayerCombatNetworkController 14/14 pass. Remaining failures in the
UtilityExpedition, PlayerEquipment, PlayerDownedReviveInteraction and
TownPartyLocalAuthority fixtures reproduce identically without this
change.

commits.subject: feat(loot): collect world pickups partially when capacity runs out
commits.body:
A pickup that does not fully fit the player's Inventory now transfers
the largest admissible quantity instead of rejecting the interaction.
The remainder stays in the same pickup with its exact Raid origins and
first-acquisition eligibility, and remains available to any player.
Zero admissible units still reject without changing the pickup, and a
complete transfer still despawns it (Doc 07 sections 11, 14 and 28).

Only capacity failures (InventoryFull, MaxTransportableExceeded,
Overflow) enter the partial path. The admissible amount is the largest
canonical, Dungeon-first prefix of the pickup's origins accepted by
both side-effect-free receiver validators, found by binary search. The
remainder's origin state is encoded before the receiver commit.
Eligibility is consumed eligible-first, and Progress, treasure
instability and pickup feedback use only the collected units. A
partial success returns Succeeded(isConsumed: false).

Add RaidLootOriginTransfer.TrySplit for exact canonical splits.

Tests:
- RaidLootOriginTransferSplitTests (EditMode, 7 cases)
- NetworkLootPickupPartialPickupPlayModeTests (PlayMode, 5 cases):
  full, partial, zero capacity, mixed-origin remainder and sequential
  competitors

Docs: LootInteractionArchitecture pickup reception section.

RaidInventoryPresenterInteraction 56/56 PlayMode pass. Pre-existing
failures are unchanged. Host/Client replication is not yet validated.

commits.subject: feat(combat): enforce friendly fire and ally 1 HP floor
commits.body:
Apply the Doc 19 section 7 Friendly Fire rules in the authoritative
damage pipeline. Allies are players on the same initial Raid team
(AbilityAllyAffiliation, fail closed); environmental and creature
damage are never ally damage.

- Friendly Fire off: DamageResolver rejects ally hits with
  FriendlyFireBlocked before the target mutates; no damage, knockback,
  aggro or contribution.
- Friendly Fire on: ally damage is scaled by the serialized
  _allyDamageMultiplier (default 1.0) and the resolver rebuilds the
  request with DamageRequest.IsAllyDirectDamage, which callers cannot
  set themselves.
- CharacterBase clamps ally damage after mitigation so Health never
  drops below 1 HP and never runs the fatal/Downed interception.
- PlayerCharacter ignores ally hits on the Downed Health reserve and
  never calls NotifyDownedDamaged, so revive is not interrupted.
- Eligible knockback still applies to an allowed ally hit whose clamped
  damage is 0. Aggro and contribution need applied damage > 0.
- AbilityImpact routes zero-damage pushes through the resolver, and
  NetworkExplosiveBomb drops its direct ApplyDamage fallback, so no
  path bypasses the policy.
- Pure decision math lives in FriendlyFireRules.

Tests:
- FriendlyFireRulesTests: blocking, multiplier, post-mitigation floor,
  non-ally and environmental damage.
- DamageResolverFriendlyFireTests: blocked ally hit, unavailable
  policy, non-ally/environmental damage, zero-damage push knockback.
- PlayerDownedPlayModeTests: multiplier and repeated ally hits stop at
  1 HP without Downed.
- PlayerDownedRecoveryPlayModeTests: ally hits keep the Downed reserve
  and assisted revive; zero-effective reviver hits do not interrupt.

Refs: TASK-245
Player-Added: Teammates can no longer hurt, push or down each other in a raid unless the host enables friendly fire, and even then they can never knock an ally down.

  runtime; callers treat an unavailable context as disabled.

commits.subject: test(combat): cover knockback resolution in PlayMode

- T04/T06 weaker or equal push keeps the active one
- Same-tick perpendicular pushes do not accumulate vectors
- T07 fatal hit downs the player and completes travel

commits.subject: feat(combat): resolve knockback with resistance and strict replacement
commits.body:
Replace the additive, friction-decayed knockback velocity with the
authoritative Doc 18 section 6 model on players and enemies. A push is
mitigated by Knockback Resistance (RE), at most one push is active per
character, and eligibility is taken from the state at impact.

- IKnockbackReceiver/IKnockbackMotor now carry a KnockbackRequest
  (direction, original PE, eligibility snapshot) and return a
  KnockbackDecision. CharacterBase applies max(0, PE - RE).
- DamageResolver snapshots IsKnockbackEligible before ApplyDamage, so a
  hit that downs an Active player still pushes; hits on an already
  Downed player never start or replace a push. Defeat cancels travel.
- Player and enemy motors keep one networked push (direction, effective
  PE, distance, start tick, duration) written by State Authority. Steps
  derive from the curve and tick, so resimulation is safe and blocked
  distance against walls is lost. Absorbed pushes do not interrupt
  abilities or bump KnockbackSequence. Restore spawns keep the state in
  Fusion's resumed tick domain; fresh spawns reset it.
- RE comes from armor (ArmorDefinition.KnockbackResistance, aggregated in
  EquipmentStatisticsModifiers, no attribute scaling) and from a
  serialized enemy value (default 0).
- Existing KnockbackForce fields are reinterpreted as original PE; no
  serialized field was renamed.
- Add KnockbackCurveConfig.asset and reference it from NetworkPlayer,
  SocialPlayer and NetworkEnemy (enemy variants inherit it). A missing
  or invalid config fails dependency validation with an error.

Tests:
- EquipmentStatisticsCalculatorTests: RE accumulates across armor and
  RE-only armor validates.
- Ability PlayMode tests migrated to TryApplyKnockback and the new
  active-push accessors.

Refs: TASK-244
Player-Improved: Knockbacks no longer stack: only a stronger hit replaces an ongoing push, armor can resist pushes, and players already downed are no longer pushed around.

commits.subject: feat(combat): add knockback power rules and curve config
commits.body:
Add the pure, allocation-free rules for Doc 18 section 6 knockback and
the ScriptableObject that converts effective push power into travel.
Nothing consumes them yet; motor integration follows separately.

- KnockbackRules: effective PE = max(0, PE - RE), strict replacement
  decision (only a strictly greater effective PE replaces the active
  push; ties keep it), eligibility snapshot at impact, continuation
  through Downed and cancellation on definitive Defeat, cumulative
  per-tick step and completion.
- KnockbackCurveConfig: effective PE to distance (0.1 m/PE, max 3 m),
  duration (0.03 s/PE clamped to [0.1, 0.5] s, ceil to ticks with a
  float tolerance) and an ease-out cumulative profile. Values are
  placeholders pending balance (Doc 18 section 9).

Tests:

  step sums, replacement restart and config validation (25/25 EditMode).

commits.subject: feat(minimap): render wall art from a 2x2 averaged tile atlas
commits.body:
The minimap draws 8 PPU tile art at about 4 screen pixels per tile, so
Point sampling kept only one of every two 1-texel rows. Wall bases lost
their light edge and showed a dark band that the Tilemap does not have.

The layout generator now bakes an alpha-weighted 2x2 box-averaged copy
of each source atlas, decoded from the original PNG bytes, and stores it
as a Point/Clamp, mip-free sub-asset of the generated layout. Batches are
rebound to that copy with their original UVs. The source PNG and its
import settings are untouched. The hash version tag is bumped to
"scene-tile-art-v3-avg2", and a layout whose batches do not reference
embedded art is regenerated, so existing layouts migrate automatically.
A failed bake writes nothing and fails the prebuild gate.

This supersedes the previous rule that the minimap samples the original
textures without a baked copy.

Tests:
- MinimapArtDownsamplerTests: exact averaging, alpha weighting,
  transparent blocks, odd sizes rejected, Point/Clamp output
- GraphicUsesTheAveragedTileAtlasGeneratedInsideTheLayout replaces the
  original-atlas identity test

commits.subject: fix(minimap): snap the map in root canvas pixels to stop wall flicker
commits.body:
The overlay HUD Canvas is parented to the moving NetworkPlayer, and
Unity does not re-centre an overlay canvas transform. Snapping the map
pivot in world space therefore assumed world == screen and left the map
at a fractional pixel equal to the player's fractional position, so the
point-sampled wall tiles blinked while moving.

Overlay canvases now round the map pivot in root-canvas pixel space
(canvas-local position minus rect origin, times scaleFactor), which is
independent of where the canvas sits in world space. Camera and world
space canvases keep the existing camera-based path.

Tests:
- MapPivotSnapsToCanvasPixelsWhenHudCanvasIsUnderAMovingParent (canvas
  scales 0.73, 1 and 1.37; failed with a 0.37 px drift before the fix)

Player-Fixed: Minimap walls no longer flicker while your character moves.

commits.subject: fix(loot): attach passive effects controller and sync drop definition
commits.body:
Convert PlayerInventoryPassiveEffectsController to a MonoBehaviour that reactively queries the replicated player inventory without consuming Fusion word budget. Attach it to NetworkPlayer.prefab and add fallback dependency resolution in PlayerCharacter.

Synchronize the serialized LootDefinition field in NetworkLootPickup when spawning or dropping items so the Unity Inspector accurately displays the resolved item definition instead of default Bone.

commits.subject: fix(loot): expand catalog index capacity in packed origin buffer
commits.body:
Expand MaximumCatalogEntries from 64 to 128 in RaidLootOriginPackedBuffer to support the expanded 81-definition catalog without exceeding network bit budget. Adjust KeyBits from 6 to 12 while preserving 43 bits per bucket and 686-word buffer allocation for NetworkPlayer.

Update PlayerLootReceiver unit tests and technical documentation in LootInteractionArchitecture.md to reflect the 128-definition ceiling.

commits.subject: feat(loot): implement inventory passive effects for expedition treasures
feat(consumables): implement mana restoration and consumption speed gates

feat(loot): implement cooperative Chaos Coin bonus loot roll
commits.body:
Implement cooperative 20% bonus loot generation for containers when any active team member (alive or Downed) carries TRE_CHAOS_COIN per Docs 07 and 14. Add ChaosCoinCarrierEvaluator to consult authoritative team presence across Solo and Duo rosters while strictly excluding corpses.

Update LootContainerContentRoller to evaluate an independent deterministic Chaos Coin roll stream (2000 basis points) isolated from Luck, allowing both bonuses to co-occur without mutating the base generation seed. Seal resolved loot sources against subsequent modifier re-evaluation.

Player-Added: Carrying the Chaos Coin now grants your team an independent 20% chance to find bonus loot when opening dungeon chests.
Refs: #615

commits.subject: feat(loot): register 39 MVP items and normalize consumable catalog
commits.body:
Create ScriptableObjects for all 39 non-equippable MVP items defined in Doc 14 (21 Resources, 8 Treasures, 8 Consumables, 2 Utilities). Normalize CON_HEALTH_POTION to 40 HP restoration over 2.5s channel time. Assign visual archetypes and register all definitions into LootDefinitionCatalog and RaidLootValueCatalog.

Add comprehensive EditMode unit tests verifying catalog integrity, non-null sprite references, exact operational attributes (ObjectValue, StackMax, MaxTransportable, Family, UseMode), and strict non-stackable rule for Treasures.

Introduce ItemUseMode and formal taxonomy properties (ObjectValue, StackMax, MaxTransportable, Family, Tags, and lifecycle flags) while preserving backward compatibility with existing equippables and serialized valuable assets.

Update LootDefinition ID regex validation to accept formal alphanumeric identifiers (e.g. CON_HEALTH_POTION), and enforce validation constraints for negative values, deprecated Quest category, and unstackable Treasure items. Add comprehensive EditMode unit tests covering all new validation gates and properties.

commits.subject: test(progression): cover XP retention for disconnected and absent defeat
commits.body:
Adds PlayMode coverage that a natural defeat while disconnected and a
confirmed-absence defeat consolidate 0% of provisional XP, a connected

Also fixes the ambient presenter fixture: outside Play Mode the
presenter writes the vignette to Volume.sharedProfile, so the test now

commits.subject: fix(commerce): reject multi-line merchant drafts before submission
commits.body:
The backend has no atomic multi-line trade endpoint, so baskets always
failed with PersistenceFailed after locking the draft. A draft with
more than one purchase or sale line is now rejected locally with
RejectedByMerchant, without reserving stock or calling the backend.

Tests:
- TownMerchantTradeSessionTests: multi-line drafts rejected before
  submission; single-line expectations updated
- TownMerchantTradePlayModeTests: multi-line draft rejected and a
  single-line trade still works

Player-Fixed: Confirming a merchant trade with more than one item is now refused right away instead of failing after the merchant accepts it.

commits.subject: fix(networking): fail closed on unverified identity and raid closure gaps
commits.body:
- Town sender resolution and remote Raid admission now reject requests
  when no verifier is configured, instead of trusting unsigned tickets
  or client-declared admission data. Offline/no-backend development
  flows can no longer admit remote peers.
- Absolute Dungeon closure selects unresolved Raiding participants
  through AbsoluteClosureRules; a participant whose canonical defeat
  cannot complete stays tracked and logs an error instead of being
  dropped while still Raiding.
- DefaultDungeonPressureConfig uses 900 s before Collapse (15 + 2 min
  total); thresholds 240/60 and Collapse 120 unchanged.
- Reconnect ticket disposal uses the attempt-local shutdown reason and
  exception, so a stale terminal reason cannot discard a recoverable
  ticket.
- RaidPlayerDeparturePolicy drops the unused decider argument.

Tests (source-grep checks replaced by behavioural tests):
- RaidAdmissionSecurityTests: inflated client claims with no verifier
  are rejected (snapshot and ticket formats)
- TownIdentitySecurityTests: unsigned ticket for a victim profile with
  no verifier is rejected
- RaidAbsoluteClosureTests: Raiding-only selection regardless of
  connectivity or Downed; default asset totals 17 minutes
- RaidReconnectClientFlowTests: exception cannot reuse a previous
  terminal reason
- RaidPlayerDepartureTests, RaidExtractionConnectivityTests,
  RaidConnectivityContinuityTests: behavioural departure and
  extraction-connectivity rules

Docs: DungeonPressure timing and unresolved-defeat handling;
RaidConnectivityContinuity marks invalid-config disconnect as a
misconfiguration fail-safe.

commits.subject: fix(extraction): keep team progress when the Host migrates
commits.body:
CopyStateFrom restored the replicated slots but left the instance
uninitialized, so the new Host's first tick re-ran roster
initialization and reset every team's progress, quota baseline and
Sanctuary request to zero. Restored state now counts as initialized.

Tests:
- TeamExtractionProgressTests: CopyStateFrom into a fresh instance
  preserves progress, Duo quota and assignment after initialization;
  an absent member does not reduce the quota or multiply contributions
- TeamExtractionRequirementRulesTests: connected required members
  inside the tolerant area keep the countdown running

commits.subject: fix(deps): pin body-parser to 2.4.0 for the compressed-body DoS
commits.body:
body-parser 2.3.0, pulled by express 5.2.1 and reachable through

commits.subject: fix(backend): remove the unlimited free shop sample
commits.body:
free_sample cost 0 gold, could be bought up to 999 per request without

commits.subject: fix(backend): keep raid reward receipts as durable replay barriers
commits.body:
Authoritative raid results expire after 24 h and extraction receipts
were evicted past 256 entries, so a consumed raid could be republished
and rewarded twice. Receipts are no longer pruned, the atomic commit
predicate rejects any existing receipt for the same raid, and
publication returns 409 RESULT_ALREADY_CONSUMED once the recipient has
a receipt for that raid.

Reviewers: receipts now grow with every extracted raid per character
(bounded by the Mongo document size).

Tests:
- extraction.authoritative: consumed raid cannot be republished after
  TTL deletion and receipt-cap pressure
- extraction.commit, inventory.extraction, raid.result updated for
  durable receipts

commits.subject: fix(backend): fail closed on missing NODE_ENV and spoofable proxy trust
commits.body:
Startup now requires an explicit NODE_ENV, so a production deploy
without it can no longer skip the production secret guards. TRUST_PROXY
accepts only false or a hop count; `true` is rejected because it lets a
client spoof X-Forwarded-For and bypass the per-IP auth limiter.

Deployments must set NODE_ENV and a numeric TRUST_PROXY (e.g. 1).
Test scripts load tests/setup.js to supply synthetic configuration
instead of the local .env.

Tests:
- env.hardening: missing NODE_ENV, TRUST_PROXY parsing and rejection
- auth.hardening.integration: register limiter 429 + Retry-After with
  spoofed forwarded headers; debug and legacy routes 404 in production
- session.revocation: login after logout issues a working token while
  the old one stays revoked

Docs: US-60 walkthrough limits, logout signature and per-process
limiter limitation corrected.

commits.subject: feat(commerce): show and confirm equipment buy-back in the merchant
commits.body:
List the account's buy-back entries after the authored stock in the
merchant grid, priced from the ledger, and confirm one entry at a time
through IBuybackService without Fusion RPCs or shared stock. A draft
that mixes buy-back with normal lines is blocked with

(ownership, eligibility, price, capacity, Town-ticket lifetime, flow)
from GD UI.1.4 7.1 and resolves known gap 3 for eligible equipment.

blocking, locking and outcomes; PlayMode sale followed by buy-back.

commits.subject: feat(commerce): hydrate and execute equipment buy-back in Unity
commits.body:
Add the client side of the per-account buy-back: DTOs and
ShopBuybackAsync, a memory-only BuybackLedger owned by the application
stash context and replaced from hydration, reconciliation and every
shop response, and a remote-first ExecuteBuybackAsync that dry-runs
gold, capacity and reservation locally, awaits the backend and applies
its authoritative totals. A new Town ticket clears the ledger, since it
starts a new backend epoch.

IBuybackEligibilityPolicy (equipment and weapons today) is a
presentation hint and the extension point for a stricter rule; the
backend stays authoritative.

Tests: buy-back success, rejection mapping, dry-run, replay, transport
loss and sale ledger replacement; ledger replacement and eligibility.

commits.subject: feat(backend): let players buy back equipment they sold this Town session
commits.body:
Selling an equipment piece now records a per-account buy-back entry
in the same atomic update as the sale, priced at ceil(sell value x
BUYBACK_PRICE_MULTIPLIER = 1.5) and capped at 16 entries, oldest
first. POST /character/me/inventory/shop/buyback rebuys from an entry
with the same receipt, reservation, revision and funds guards as the
shop. Issuing a Town session ticket starts a new buy-back epoch.

Eligibility is LootCategory 5-10 behind isBuybackEligible so a later
rule can replace it; the parity test checks it against the Unity
assets.

Tests: unit guard order and replay; MongoMemoryServer coverage for
FIFO, partial and full consumption, account isolation, epoch expiry
and write races.

commits.subject: test(commerce): cover merchant trades end to end in PlayMode
commits.body:
Drive the real TownMerchantNPC prefab through Fusion RPCs in a single
runner with an in-memory profile and a controlled backend seam, so the
chain from the trade session to stock, profile and UI feedback runs in
CI without network access.

Tests: RPC ticket round trip; acknowledged purchase; rejected sale
keeping profile and stock; insufficient gold disabling Confirm; second
Confirm refused while the backend is pending; multi-line ticket
releasing stock.

commits.subject: docs(commerce): record E2E re-run after remote-first persistence
docs(commerce): note persistence tests run only in PlayMode
fix(commerce): report trade outcomes only after backend acknowledgement
commits.body:
Trades committed locally and synced fire-and-forget, so the merchant
authority consumed or restocked shared stock for trades the backend
later rejected, and the panel kept saying the trade succeeded.
ExecuteTradeAsync now dry-runs the ticket, awaits the backend and
commits locally only on acknowledgement; the trade session reports the
real outcome and keeps Confirm locked until then, which also stops a
quick second trade from sending a stale revision.

Also guard the merchant RPC handlers against a missing validator, fail
loudly when BackendConfiguration is missing, and correct the retry
claims in the service docs. A lost response still reports the trade as
not persisted; CommerceArchitecture.md records that gap.

Tests: RemoteShopTransactionServiceTests (acknowledgement, rejection
mapping, dry-run, transport loss, multi-line refusal) and session
tests for acknowledgement timing, serialization and disposal.

commits.subject: fix(commerce): reject trades while a raid reservation is pending
commits.body:
TryCommitTrade skipped the Town mutation gate, so a trade during a
pending Raid loadout reservation could fill capacity and leave the
reservation impossible to roll back. New trades now return
ReservationPending, matching the backend 409 RESERVATION_PENDING;
already-applied receipts still replay as AlreadyApplied.

Tests: reservation rejection with rollback restoring the loadout,
receipt replay during a reservation, and ReservationPending in the
trade session rejection cases.

commits.subject: docs(commerce): record E2E results against Render
commits.body:
Editor E2E with a dedicated account confirms H3, H4, H5 and M3 at
runtime and adds E1 (success feedback after a rejected trade), E2
(sold non-offered items are not re-buyable, GD vs contract) and E3 (a
Fusion assert after leaving Play Mode).

commits.subject: docs(commerce): propose durable ability purchases and atomic trades
commits.body:
Design options for audit findings H1 (backend-owned ability unlocks
priced server-side), H3 (single atomic multi-line trade endpoint with
server-side capacity) and C1 (raid result trust without a
client-held secret), with the decisions each one needs.

commits.subject: fix(backend): mirror Unity loot prices in the shop catalog
commits.body:
Unity LootDefinition assets are the price source. Armor set pieces
were sellable in Unity but rejected by the backend with
ITEM_NOT_SELLABLE, while arming_sword and shield were tradable only on
the backend. Remove those offers and the unreachable training_sword
and duplicate health_potion keys, and add the armor sell values.

Tests: a parity test compares every LootDefinition asset with the
catalogs and skips when the Unity folder is absent; integration
fixtures now use healthpotion.

commits.subject: fix(backend): reject shop trades while a raid reservation is pending
commits.body:
Buying during a pending reservation put items into the emptied
loadout, so a rollback silently dropped the reserved items and the
extraction commit failed with LOADOUT_NOT_EMPTY. shopBuy and shopSell
now answer 409 RESERVATION_PENDING, also guard the atomic update, and
still replay already-applied receipts.

Tests: unit and MongoMemoryServer coverage for buy/sell rejection,
receipt replay during a reservation and a reservation created between
read and write.

commits.subject: docs(commerce): record raid result signing secret exposure
commits.body:
Add C1 to the commerce audit: the raid-result HMAC secret ships in
the client BackendConfiguration asset and the Render backend accepts
it, so any authenticated player can mint items and experience.

commits.subject: docs(commerce): add commerce system audit report
commits.body:
Record the read-only audit of the Town Merchant, shop persistence,
backend shop and Ability Vendor against CommerceArchitecture.md and

commits.subject: feat(town): replicate full prepared equipment for inspection
commits.body:
Extends the SocialPlayer equipment source so every Town peer receives
the full prepared Equipment of each member, which the Preparation
screen needs to inspect another member read-only.

  prepared slots (both Weapon Sets plus body armor) as catalog

commits.subject: feat(inventory): add manual sort, reserved 2H slot and Downed lock
commits.body:
Completes the inventory functions required by the UI audit (3b.9 to
3b.12). No inventory surface sorts itself anymore: a Sort button on
the Stash and Loadout panels and on the shared Town/Raid inventory
applies the existing category-then-name rule only when pressed, and
new items append at the end.

- Stash and Loadout show their stored order. Sort is a LocalProfileStore
  permutation transaction sent remote-first through the order endpoint
  and the serialized StashTransferCoordinator queue; it is rejected
  while a reservation is pending and allowed while Ready. Take All and
  Leave All follow the stored order.
- The coordinator is now owned by ApplicationStashContext so the Stash
  screen and the Town inventory share one queue per profile.
- Raid keeps a presentation-local order seeded from the reserved
  Loadout; it is not replicated and not carried back on extraction.
- The Off Hand of a Set holding a two-handed weapon shows that weapon
  dimmed as reserved and refuses drops; the active Weapon Set is
  highlighted and the inactive one dimmed.
- While Downed the Raid inventory stays visible but read-only, with a
  visible reason, and recovers without reopening.
- Prefabs: Sort buttons added to StashInventory and RaidInventoryUI.

Tests:
- StashTransferCoordinatorTests, StashDisplayOrderTests: order
  transaction, remote-first Sort, reconciliation, stored bulk order,
  shared queue ownership.
- RaidInventoryDisplayOrderTests, DropPolicyTests: local order
  maintenance and reserved Off Hand refusal.
- Lobby Stash and Raid inventory PlayMode tests: Sort buttons, reserved
  slot, Set visuals and the Downed read-only block.

Docs: RaidInventoryUIArchitecture.md and
LocalPlayerPersistenceArchitecture.md document the order contract, the
queue ownership and the Downed block; the compact no-hole model is
recorded as approved design debt against GD 16 section 3.

Refs: TASK-218
Player-Added: Inventories and the Stash now have a Sort button, and items stay in the order you leave them.
Player-Improved: A two-handed weapon now shows its second hand slot as reserved, and the active weapon set is easy to spot.
Player-Improved: While downed you can still look at your inventory, but it clearly tells you it cannot be changed.

commits.subject: feat(backend): persist player-controlled inventory order
commits.body:
Adds an authenticated order write so the Stash and Loadout keep the
order the player chose instead of being sorted for display. The
backend stores the reordered array; no position field is added to
the item schema.

Contract: PUT /character/me/inventory/order with
{ list: "stash" | "loadout", lootIds, expectedRevision }. The list
must be an exact permutation of the current array (amounts kept,
other list untouched). Rejects with 409 RESERVATION_PENDING while a
reservation exists, 409 REVISION_CONFLICT on a stale or racing
revision, and 400 VALIDATION_FAILED for a malformed or mismatched
order. Returns { stash, loadout, revision } like the move routes.

Tests:
- inventory.order.test.js: stash and loadout reorder, invalid
  permutations, stale revision, pending reservation, atomic race and
  request validation.

Refs: TASK-218

commits.subject: fix(player): align player action rules with Game Design
commits.body:
Correct four player behaviors that contradicted Game Design 04, 08 and
17 (TASK-221). Rules are enforced on the authoritative side, not only
in presentation.

- Attribute maximum is 30 (04 s8/s11, 08 s4) in Unity
  ProgressionBalanceDefaults and backend MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE. Loaders
  never clamp, so profiles at 25 keep loading and can rise to 30.
- Attribute assignment is rejected while Ready (04 s10/s12). New
  TownAttributeMutationEndpoint checks TownEquipmentMutationGate before
  the store, so a blocked attempt never reaches the backend commit. The
  panel disables every assignment while Ready and refreshes on open and
  after a blocked attempt.
- Sprint is suppressed every tick while a weapon attack or ability
  executes (17 s5/s9): no sprint speed, stamina spend or rejection
  telemetry. Held Sprint resumes when the action ends; base movement is
  unchanged.
- A basic attack during an executing ability is rejected with the new
  AttackFailureReason.AbilityInProgress (appended), on status,
  authoritative acceptance and the legacy path, without cancelling or
  queuing the ability (17 s7.3/s9).

Reviewers should verify: the Ready gate lives at the Unity mutation
boundary because the backend has no Ready state; movement (-10) runs
before combat (-7), so Sprint still applies on the attack start tick;
ability start during a basic attack remains a TASK-223 follow-up.

Tests: attribute maximum and former-maximum progression (Unity and
backend), TownAttributeMutationEndpoint Ready gate, presentation and
binding Ready refresh, sprint suppression during execution, and basic
attack rejection during an ability without cancel or queue.

Docs: PlayerMovement, PlayerCombat, AbilitySystem and Progression
architecture.

Player-Balanced: Each attribute can now be raised up to 30 instead of 25.
Player-Fixed: Attribute points can no longer be spent while you are marked as Ready for an expedition.
Player-Fixed: Attacking or using an ability while sprinting now stops the sprint, and you can no longer start sprinting in the middle of an attack.

  in both hands (Main +135 -> -45 deg, Off reflected across the facing
  axis), keeping source timing and authored recovery endpoints; slash
  VFX poses recalibrated and reflected across the facing axis;
- two-handed secondary-grip weapons keep the left hand on the handle in
  idle, walk and attacks; bow holder hand sorts behind the body facing
  north; main-hand shield Defend keeps the right hand on the shield.

Reviewers should verify: Spellbook handedness contradicts GD-09 section 5

commits.subject: fix(extraction): reserve each Sanctuary exclusively for one team
commits.body:
Game Design 06 sections 10 and 12 reserve a Sanctuary for its owning
team and select only among free Sanctuaries. The assignment service
selected among every registered Sanctuary and ExtractionSanctuary
accepted a second team in a free slot (former divergence D-3), so two
teams could be assigned the same Sanctuary.

Selection now filters unreserved Sanctuaries in ascending identity
order into a reused buffer and applies the existing seeded policy to
the free count. When none is free, assignment fails closed with the
existing NoFreeSanctuary reason and the team keeps its pending request.
TryAssignTeam rejects a team while another holds a slot; the owner's
reservation stays idempotent and the networked slot layout is unchanged.

TeamExtractionProgress retries a pending request every tick, so
NoSanctuariesConfigured, NoFreeSanctuary, ReservationConflict and
existing-assignment failures are reported once per Raid generation and
retried attempts log nothing.

Tests:
- EditMode: TryAssignTeam_ReservesTheSanctuaryExclusivelyForItsOwningTeam,
  TryGetAssignment_ResolvesEachTeamToItsExclusiveSanctuary and the
  adapted ritual interaction case replace the D-3 sharing tests.
- PlayMode: the distinct-Sanctuary case forces a colliding session seed
  so exclusivity is exercised on every run; a new exhaustion case and
  the no-Sanctuary case assert that retries stay silent.

ExtractionArchitecture.md replaces D-3 with the exclusive reservation
contract and records that Level Design must provide one Sanctuary per
team until Game Design defines exhaustion.

remaining raiding participants to definitive defeat rather than aborting
the match prematurely. When the 2-minute Collapse countdown elapses,
connected and disconnected raiders are definitively resolved, generating

commits.body:

feedback: hover and press scale on buttons and toggles, fade
transitions when panels open and close, success and rejection pulses
on confirmed results, and a full-screen fade between scenes. Nothing
is networked or persisted, and no component changes Time.timeScale,

  UiPanelVisibility.SetVisible/IsVisible instead of SetActive/activeSelf.

  Systems.prefab and only observes StateChanged.

  Toggles authored in UI prefabs and open scenes (idempotent).
- Prefabs were updated by the installer and by re-serializing the UI
  prefabs, so the diffs are large and mostly additive.

this commit.

commits.subject: feat(inventory): add the four player Quick Slots
commits.body:
Implement TASK-214 (#563). A Quick Slot references a loot definition,
never a stack, so assigning, moving or clearing one never touches item
identity, Origin, amount or location. Players can use a consumable with
a shortcut without opening the Inventory.

- Bindings live in the local profile (schema 9, local only, empty when
  loading older schemas) and survive Town -> Raid -> Town. Changing them
  is not blocked by Ready or a pending reservation.
- LootDefinition gets QuickSlotCompatible, valid only with a
  ConsumableDefinition. The Health Potion is the first compatible item.
- QuickSlotController validates assignment against the inventory the
  player is looking at and unassigns a slot when its last unit is seen
  leaving. QuickSlotReleaseGate keeps bindings through extraction,
  defeat, voluntary abandon, Downed and reservations.
- Shortcuts 1-4 go through PlayerConsumableNetworkController, so they
  share the Inventory's authoritative validation and rejections. They
  never fire while gameplay input is suppressed (Inventory or menus).
- Consumption now spends Player-origin units before Dungeon ones, also
  from the Inventory. The selection order is separate from the canonical
  bucket order, so RaidLootOriginTransfer validation is unchanged.
- Assignment by drag or context menu in the Inventory (Raid and Town);
  a provisional four-slot HUD row in NetworkPlayer.prefab.
- Weapon Set A/B moved from keys 1/2 to mouse wheel up/down.

Verify: the Inventory screen prefab (RaidInventoryUI.prefab) is not part
of this commit, so the four inventory slot views are still unassigned
there. The HUD and inventory layouts are provisional and not checked in
the Game view. Host/Client consumption is not yet validated.

Tests: assignment rules, controller (amounts, depletion, transient
empty inventory), release gate, schema 9 codec and store, Origin
selection order, DropPolicy and HUD prefab wiring. The corrupt-login
recovery tests now derive schema versions from CurrentSchemaVersion.

Docs: RaidMainHud, RaidInventoryUI, LocalPlayerPersistence and
LootInteraction architectures.

commits.subject: fix(tilemap): pack the provisional tileset into a padded sprite atlas
commits.body:
Thin dashed lines flickered over the Gameplay tilemap while the camera
moved. The 8x8 provisional tileset has no spacing between tiles, and
the camera maps one texel to a non-integer number of screen pixels, so
point sampling at a tile edge could read the neighboring tile (e.g. the
brick wall edge bleeding into the floor tile). Vision Fog was not
involved: the lines also appear with the fog renderer disabled.

Add a Sprite Atlas V2 for the tileset with 4 px padding. The packer
extrudes each tile's border into the padding, so edge samples stay on
the same tile.

Atlas settings to verify: padding 4, tight packing and rotation off,
Point filter, no mipmaps, uncompressed, included in build. The source
PNG, its sprites and GUIDs, the camera and Vision Fog are unchanged.

Validated in Play Mode with a camera glide test (fog off, 4 glides x 40
frames): 1688x807 went from 6/149 frames with seams to 0/160, 1920x1080
from 1/149 to 0/160; a static frame comparison shows an identical
tilemap.

(TASK-190 part 1), replacing per-player replicated progress with a
shared networked pool and turning PlayerExtractionProgressController
into a forwarder.

Reviewers should verify:
- TeamExtractionProgress (NetworkBehaviour on NetworkMatchController)
  maintains [Networked, Capacity(16)] NetworkArray<TeamProgressSlot>.
- TeamProgressSlot is an INetworkStruct storing TeamIdRaw,
  CurrentProgress, AssignmentRequested, and InitialTeamSize; quota is
  derived dynamically from ExtractionConfig and never replicated.
- EntityRegistry manages ITeamExtractionProgress capability with
  isolated registration and runner-scoped singleton lookup.
- NetworkSpawnManager exposes TryGetRaidTeamRoster projections from
  launch context.
- PlayerExtractionProgressController validates vitality, tick, and
  authority locally, then forwards contributions to team progress.
  Individual [Networked] properties are removed in favor of snapshot
  delegates.
- Documented intermediate state: completedQuota continues to trigger
  individual sanctuary assignment until team assignment in Stage 4.
- SessionConnectionCoordinator exposes _developmentTeamSize to group
  direct development cohorts into teams of N (default 0 preserves
  Team 1 for all).

Tests added and verified:
- TeamExtractionProgressTests: solo/duo quota derivation, single pool
  accumulation, saturation at quota, isolated team pools, and invalid
  contribution rejection.
- PlayerExtractionProgressForwarderTests: forwarder snapshot
  delegation, quota fallback, and assignment trigger.
- ExtractionProgressRegistryTests: registration, conflict rejection,
  and singlet lookup for ITeamExtractionProgress.
- ExtractionProgressPrefabTests: NetworkMatchController prefab baked
  TeamExtractionProgress component with ExtractionConfig reference.

commits.subject: fix(stash): accept over-capacity backend data and stop hydrating in place
commits.body:
The backend has no Loadout slot limit, but the save codec rejected more
than 30 slots on every round-trip, so one over-capacity reconcile made
every later Commit fail. Login also hydrated repository.Snapshot in place
without saving it.

- Drop the 30-slot check from LocalProfileSaveCodec: capacity is a Store
  rule. Store operations that need a new slot already return InventoryFull,
  so the excess can only shrink.
- TryCreateLoadoutReservation refuses an over-capacity Loadout with
  InventoryFull so the excess never enters a raid.
- HydrateSnapshot validates the whole payload before writing: unknown
  LootIds and non-positive amounts are skipped, duplicates merged, and an
  amount overflow or negative currency rejects it without changes.
- Login hydrates a clone and persists it through TrySave.
- Document hydration and capacity in LocalPlayerPersistenceArchitecture.md.

commits.subject: fix(stash): keep one Stash action queue across screen reopen
commits.body:
- LobbyStashPresenter rebuilt its StashTransferCoordinator on every
  OnEnable, so closing the screen while a transfer waited for the backend
  and reopening it started a second queue that ran ahead of the first.
- Keep the coordinator and rebuild it only when the profile or one of the
  service instances changes (a logout replaces them).
- Cover it with a Play Mode test that gates a backend call, reopens the
  screen and checks the second action waits; document the lifecycle in the
  Raid inventory UI architecture and record the U2 evidence and the
  corrected branch base in the Stash hardening tracking document.

commits.subject: feat(stash): coordinate Stash actions through a serialized, pre-checked queue
commits.body:
- Move every Stash screen action (transfers, Take All / Leave All, equip,
  unequip) out of the presenter into StashTransferCoordinator, which runs
  them through one queue so an equip never interleaves with a transfer
  that is waiting for the backend, and removes the presenter's async void
  handlers.
- Add dry-run evaluators to the Store and IPlayerLoadoutService so a
  transfer the Store would refuse never reaches the backend; a move into
  a full Inventory now reports StashOperationResult.InventoryFull instead
  of PersistenceFailed.
- Put the remote inventory service and the reconciliation service behind
  interfaces, and share the Town Ready gate between the Inventory and
  Stash screens through TownEquipmentMutationGate.
- Cover the evaluators, the coordinator (order, reconciliation, queue)
  and the real Stash prefab end to end; document the flow in the Raid
  inventory UI architecture.

commits.subject: fix(stash): reject Stash and Equipment mutations while a reservation is pending
commits.body:
- A pending raid reservation owns Inventory and Equipment, but Stash
  transfers, equip-from-Stash and equipment assign/clear still ran. A
  later rollback overwrote their result (one unit lost in the repro) and
  a non-empty Loadout made the extraction commit fail.
- Gate those operations behind one Store helper that returns the new
  StashOperationResult.ReservationPending without changing or publishing
  anything, and make the transfers fail with InvalidInventory instead of
  throwing when the profile is unavailable.
- Cover every gated operation, the unit-conservation and extraction
  regressions, the lifted invariant after rollback and the unavailable
  profile; document the invariant in the persistence architecture.

commits.body:

forced definitive defeat flow (TASK-189) when a participant's reconnect
budget is exhausted.

before executing definitive defeat without synthetic damage or Kill XP.

confirmed absence. Re-connection requests for abandoned profiles are
rejected as terminal. The duo HUD exposes the decision button on budget
exhaustion, updates presentation to reflect abandoned status, and the

session recovery.

captured aim. An invalid position is a normal rejection with no payment,
sequence or cooldown. Composed on the player prefab with placeholder balance

source EntityId.

execution is accepted, and commits it in AbilityExecutionSnapshot next to
the sequence, phase and cooldown. Behaviors receive it through the
snapshot, so Rebind and Host Migration restore it without re-reading.

  unusable direction rejects as AimUnavailable with no cost or cooldown.
- Clear the captured aim when the execution stops, after Stop receives it.
- Wire the movement controller on NetworkPlayer.prefab and validate it in
  Spawned().

  fallback, rejection, stop, state copy) with tests.

It also updates deferred implementation scope and references to the live targeting gameplay document.

commits.subject: fix(combat): apply player melee damage on an authoritative release tick
commits.body: Player melee now follows the ranged release model. Acceptance validates the swing, starts the cooldown and commits a networked MeleeAttackRelease; damage resolves when the release tick is reached, with the origin sampled at release and the weapon identity checked. A pending swing blocks new acceptance and is cancelled by downed, disabled, phase exit or weapon change. A zero delay still resolves on the acceptance tick. Melee presentation enters the timed path through HasReleaseTimeline.

commits.subject: refactor(combat): generalize weapon release seconds to all attacks
commits.body: Rename WeaponDefinition._rangedReleaseSeconds to _attackReleaseSeconds (FormerlySerializedAs keeps existing assets loading) and expose it as AttackReleaseSeconds. The configured release delay is now passed to every attack's execution parameters, not only ranged ones. Existing melee assets keep a zero delay, so behavior is unchanged.

commits.subject: fix(movement): depenetrate kinematic motor from initial wall overlaps
commits.body:
Knockback could leave a character overlapping the wall tilemap. With
queriesStartInColliders enabled, every cast started inside the wall hit
at distance zero, so the motor blocked all movement and the character
stayed stuck.

Kinematic2DMovementMotor.Move now resolves initial overlaps against the
collision mask before sweeping, also when the requested displacement is
zero. The correction is excluded from the returned displacement so it
does not affect IsMoving or facing.

Add EditMode coverage for overlap recovery and the wall-stop regression,
and document the responsibility in PlayerMovementArchitecture.

Tests:

commits.subject: refactor(animation): remove the unused LegacyRanged attack route
commits.body:
No catalog weapon selects the LegacyRanged route any longer: every
weapon attacks through the generic Attack state driven by its
DirectionalAttackAnimationSet. Remove the dead route and the weapon
animation category that only existed to select it.

- Character.controller: drop the LegacyRanged-Attack state, its
  LegacyRanged-Attack-Directional BlendTree, its AnyState and exit
  transitions, and the WeaponAnimationCategory parameter. The
  RightHand layer keeps a single AnyState route to Attack
  (OnAttack && HasGenericAttack).
- Delete the WeaponAnimationCategory enum and remove
  _animationCategory, its accessor and its validation from
  WeaponDefinition.PresentationConfig and the 11 weapon definitions.
- PlayerAnimatorView drives attack presentation from HasGenericAttack
  and the attack-set overrides only; RefreshWeaponAnimationCategory
  becomes RefreshAttackAnimation.
- Keep the MagicWand_Attack_* clips: the Wand attack set still uses

Tests:
- The controller has no WeaponAnimationCategory parameter, only the
  Attack state, and a single AnyState transition to it.
- CatalogWeapons_UseOnlyTheGenericAttackRoute: every catalog weapon
  has a complete attack set and no weapon asset serializes
  _animationCategory.
- ConfirmedCatalogIdentity_UsesItsOwnGenericAnimation now covers all

- The six-direction one-shot clip check reads the Wand attack set

as the only attack route and drops the category references.

commits.subject: feat(vfx): add Bow Shot attack VFX with Compound Bow release alignment
commits.body:
Compound Bow now plays the Bow Shot on its release. Its own
CompoundBowBowShotAttackVfx aligns the existing BowShotVfxVisual with
the Compound Bow attack, so both bows share one art asset and each
keeps its own alignment. PlayerAttackVfxPresenter and all runtime code
are unchanged.

- Starts at 0.4 s, the end of the Compound Bow stringing sequence, when
  the string hand leaves the hold; the 0.2 s shot ends inside every
  0.8 s attack clip.
- Each facing anchors WeaponPose at that release in its own baked clip,

- Reach offset 0.09375: from the (0, 0.09375) grip to the limb's front

Tests (Long Bow cases generalized over both bows):
- each bow references its own profile over the shared visual
- start matches the stringing release; blade reach never moves the shot
