commits.subject: feat(animation): migrate Compound Bow to a weapon-driven directional attack
commits.body:
Compound Bow leaves the LegacyRanged fallback and plays the generic
Attack route through its own DirectionalAttackAnimationSet, baked by
the existing weapon-driven rig: WeaponPose owns the bow, the left hand
holds its grip and the right hand draws the string. The WeaponDriven
contract is reused unchanged; the bow only adds its own geometry and
clips.

- DirectionalAnimationGenerator.GenerateAssets takes an optional source
  name, so Compound Bow bakes from RecurveBow_Attack.anim (left
  untouched) into CompoundBow_Attack_<Facing> clips. New menu item:
  Tools/Animations/Generate Compound Bow Directional Attacks.
- CompoundBowWeaponDefinition: category None, CompoundBow set,
  Rig WeaponDriven, SecondHand FollowsAuthoredMotion, AngleCorrection
  -90 and GripPoint (0, 0.09375), the center of the three-row limb on
  the center column of the 23x6 px RecurveBow.png.
- The clip keeps its authored timing: 0.6 s plus the 0.1 s blends on
  each side (0.8 s). It is not stretched to the 1.8 s attack interval.
- Recurve draws to chest height, so its lower aim center brings the
  north-facing bow closer to the body than Long Bow's.
- No catalog weapon uses LegacyRanged any longer; the route is kept
  and its removal is a separate follow-up.

Tests (Long Bow cases generalized over both bows):
- complete six-clip set and stable regeneration
- two-handed generic Attack with WeaponDriven rig
- grip derived from the sprite, shot along the facing in all facings
- WeaponPose/hand invariants, south reconstructs the source
- bow projected toward the target; draw and release read from the
  authored hold
- catalog and animator expectations moved from LegacyRanged to None

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture describes Compound Bow on the
weapon-driven rig, its geometry, timing and the unused LegacyRanged
route.

commits.subject: feat(vfx): add Bow Shot attack VFX with Long Bow release alignment
commits.body:
Long Bow now plays a Bow Shot impulse on its confirmed attack. The shot
starts at the string release that the stringing sequence already
defines, and leaves the bow's front along its shooting axis in all six
facings. It does not use a fabricated blade tip.

Generalize attack VFX sizing so it no longer always needs a blade:
- AttackVfxVisualDefinition declares UsesWeaponReach, which defaults to
  true. Such visuals keep resolving from ReachOffset + BladeReach, so
  Slash, Thrust and Cast Flash resolve exactly as before.
- A visual that does not use the weapon reach resolves from its pose's
  ReachOffset alone. WeaponDefinition requires a blade tip distinct
  from the grip point only for visuals that use the weapon reach.
- PlayerAttackVfxPresenter is unchanged. It has no branch per visual
  type or per weapon.

Add BowShotVfxVisualDefinition, reusable release impulse art:
- UsesWeaponReach is false. Its Origin, in sprite local units, sits on
  the shot origin in every frame.
- The art points along the pose axis at native pixel scale and mirrors
  across it like the bow. It is an impulse, not a trajectory, so
  neither the blade reach nor the projectile's range sizes it.

Fix the VFX-BowShot.png import to match the art:
- The sheet is four 96x96 px cells, the same layout as the other VFX
  sheets: release flash, streak, rings and remnants, traveling along
  +X on one axis. The old slicing (8x9 and 223x19) cut frame 0 and
  merged the other three frames into one sprite.
- Four centered cells at 16 PPU, point filtering, no compression.
- The flash center, (-0.875, -0.03125), is the shared origin.
- BowShotVfx.anim plays the four frames at 50 ms each on
  AttackVfx/SpriteRenderer.m_Sprite, once, over 0.2 s.

LongBowBowShotAttackVfx aligns the visual with the Long Bow:
- It starts at 0.45 s, the EndSeconds of the stringing sequence, when
  the string hand releases. The stringing stays the single source of
  that timing. The shot ends at 0.65 s, inside every 0.9 s clip.
- Each facing anchors the bow's pivot at the release, sampled from the
  baked clips: the grip on WeaponPose, rotated to the facing's shooting
  axis.
- ReachOffset is 0.09375, the distance from the grip to the limb's
  front edge in LongBow.png, the same in every facing.
- NW and SW are mirrored like the bow. Sorting is 21 in front facings
  and -9 in north facings.
- No per-direction offsets and no blade tip are configured.

Tests:
- BowShotPresentationTests: import and cell layout; origin derived from
  the flash; the clip; only Bow Shot ignores the weapon reach;
  reach-based VFX resolve as before; Long Bow validates without a
  blade and blade reach never moves or resizes the shot; start tied to
  the stringing release; poses re-derived from the prefab in six
  facings; the real presenter LateUpdate shows nothing before 0.45 s,
  frames 0-3 until 0.65 s, then clears; the confirmed effect survives
  an equipment lookup failure mid-attack.
- DirectionalAttackAnimationSetTests now expects the Long Bow Bow Shot
  VFX. RejectedAttack_ClearsPendingEffect uses Compound Bow as the
  weapon without a VFX.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md documents UsesWeaponReach, the Bow
Shot visual and the Long Bow alignment.

commits.subject: feat(animation): animate Long Bow string draw during its attack
commits.body:
Long Bow now draws, holds and releases its string during the confirmed
attack. The frames follow the same baked attack clip that drives
WeaponPose and both hands. Only the held weapon's sprite changes: its
pose, GripPoint, AngleCorrection, facing and mirror are unchanged.

Add WeaponAttackSpriteAnimation, an optional presentation asset
referenced from WeaponDefinition.Presentation.AttackSpriteAnimation:
- StartSeconds in attack clip time, plus ordered frames of a sprite
  and a positive duration.
- Validation requires a complete attack animation set and a sequence
  that ends inside all six attack clips.
- Before the start, after the last frame and outside the attack, the
  weapon shows its world sprite. Weapons without the asset behave as
  before.

Runtime stays generic and local:
- PlayerAnimatorView.TryGetPresentedAttackSeconds returns the clip time
  only while the RightHand layer plays an Attack state whose clip
  belongs to the pinned attack weapon's own set.
- PlayerWeaponPresenter resolves the frame through
  PlayerWeaponPresentationMath.ResolveMainHandSprite and swaps only the
  renderer sprite. It adds no Animator, layer, controller, networked
  state or weapon identity branch. The attack VFX pipeline is untouched.

Long Bow stringing sheet:
- The sheet was drawn rotated 90 degrees from the world sprite: frame 0
  rotated counter-clockwise is pixel-identical to LongBow.png. Rotate it
  in place so the frames share the world sprite's orientation,
  AngleCorrection (-90) and GripPoint (0, 0.125).
- Import settings: 16 PPU, point filtering, no compression, tight frame
  rects, and custom pivots on the center column 3.5 px below the top of
  the limb, so the grip lands on the same pixel in every frame.
- LongBowStringingAttackSpriteAnimation starts at 0.1 s, when the
  ease-in ends. Frames: rest 0.10-0.20, partial draws 0.20-0.25 and
  0.25-0.35, full draw and hold 0.35-0.45. The string releases at
  0.45 s, when the string hand leaves the hold. One sequence serves all
  six facings.

Tests (WeaponAttackSpriteAnimationTests):
- frame window boundaries and validation rules;
- every weapon except Long Bow has no attack sprite animation;
- Long Bow references its asset, timing and frames and keeps its
  weapon-driven pose values;
- every frame keeps 16 PPU, point filtering and the grip on the center
  of the limb, and frame 0 matches the world sprite pixel for pixel;
- presenter on NetworkPlayer.prefab with the real Animator: the sprite
  changes in sync with the attack clip time while the weapon visual's
  position, rotation and scale stay unchanged, and Idle falls outside
  the attack window;
- a clip outside the pinned weapon's set never plays its frames;
- presenter, math, animator view and asset code do not depend on the
  weapon's identity.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md documents the contract and the Long
Bow configuration.

commits.subject: feat(animation): migrate Long Bow to a weapon-driven directional attack
commits.body:
Bake the south-authored LongBow_Attack.anim into six one-shot
directional clips (N, NE, NW, S, SE, SW). Add a LongBow
DirectionalAttackAnimationSet and move the bow from LegacyRanged to the
generic Attack route (category None).

The authored clip shows a right-handed archer. The left hand is the bow
arm and pushes toward the target. The right hand draws the string toward
the face and releases it. A rigid bow sprite cannot follow a hand-held
rig, so add WeaponRig to WeaponDefinition.Presentation:
- HandHeld (default): the single weapon visual follows MainHandGrip.
  Every other weapon is unchanged.
- WeaponDriven: the weapon owns its pose. PlayerWeaponPresenter
  reparents the same visual to WeaponPose, a new transform under
  VisualRoot that sits inside no hand. Validation allows it only for
  two-handed weapons whose second hand is FollowsAuthoredMotion.

Weapon-driven bake contract:
- The south source is read as drawn positions: each hand transform
  plus its idle sprite anchor.
- The left hand becomes the WeaponPose trajectory and the right hand
  becomes the string target. Both turn with the facing about the aim
  center: the body axis at the string-hand height of the authored
  draw hold. This keeps the aim height, so N draws upward instead of
  toward the feet.
- Both runtime hands are keyed so their drawn centroids land on those
  points. The bow hand always holds the grip, and the string hand
  never moves the bow. South reproduces the source exactly.
- The clip eases in from, and back out to, the facing's locomotion pose
  over 0.1 s on each side, because the source starts in a ready pose and
  the Attack transitions are instant. The clip is 0.9 s long, matching
  the bow's attack interval.
- In S, SE and SW the bow hand sorts at 25: over the bow (20) and its
  VFX (21), under the main hand (30).

Outside attacks, WeaponPose rests in the drawn left hand. The new
"Generate Weapon Pose Locomotion" menu keys it in every Idle and Walk
clip at each LeftHand sprite frame.

Long Bow configuration, derived from the 27x7 px LongBow.png:
- GripPoint (0, 0.125): the center of the limb in the center column.
- AngleCorrection -90: the sprite shoots along +Y.

LegacyRanged remains only for Compound Bow.

Tests:
- Weapon-driven clip contract in six facings: grip invariant, aim-center
  turn, authored timing and rotation art, locomotion rest at both ends,
  forward-of-body invariant, and bow-hand sorting.
- WeaponPose locomotion keys in all Idle and Walk clips.
- HandHeld outputs do not animate WeaponPose.
- WeaponDriven validation.
- LongBow set, GripPoint derived from the sprite pixels, and presenter
  orientation in six facings.
- Prefab hierarchy with a single weapon visual and WeaponPose outside
  the hands.
- Catalog and Animator expectations for Long Bow on generic Attack.

Document the weapon rig in PlayerCombatArchitecture.md.

commits.subject: feat(vfx): add Cast Flash attack VFX with Magic Staff alignment
commits.body:
Make Magic Staff the second consumer of the shared CastFlashVfxVisual
through its own MagicStaffCastFlashAttackVfx alignment. The art, the
clip and the presenter are reused unchanged, and the Cast Flash
contract needed no changes.

Derived from MagicStaff.png and the six staff directional clips:
- BladeTip (-0.0625, 0.53125): the center of the 5x5 px gem of the
  13x24 px sprite. Reach from the grip is 1.0331.
- The cast is at 0.9s in every facing, when the forward strike peaks.
  startSeconds 0.875 ignites frame 0 as the gem arrives, and frames
  2-3 fade in place while the staff recovers.
- Each pose anchors the main-hand grip at the peak and uses the grip
  to gem axis as its rotation, with no reach offset. Sorting is 21 in
  front facings and -9 in north facings, just above the held staff.

The staff's left hand is an independent authored gesture outside the
main-hand chain, so it never moves the cast point.

Generalize the Cast Flash tests per caster (Wand and Staff) and add
tests for:
- the staff configuration;
- the shared visual with independent alignments;
- tip alignment in all six facings;
- cast point independence from the left hand.

RejectedAttack_ClearsPendingEffect now uses Long Bow as its weapon
without VFX. Document the staff alignment in PlayerCombatArchitecture.md.

commits.subject: feat(animation): migrate Magic Staff to generic directional attack
commits.body:
Bake the south-authored MagicStaff_Attack.anim into six one-shot
directional clips (N, NE, NW, S, SE, SW). Add a MagicStaff
DirectionalAttackAnimationSet and move the staff from LegacyRanged to
the generic Attack route (category None).

Being two-handed does not imply that the second hand holds the weapon.
In the staff source the left hand is an independent spell gesture: it
rests on its own side of the body, rotates against the main hand and
never reaches the handle. Long Sword and Zweihander author it turning
rigidly with the main hand on the handle.

Add SecondHandPresentation to WeaponDefinition.Presentation as static
presentation data read only by the generator:
- HoldsSecondaryGrip (default): the existing handle constraint, so
  Long Sword and Zweihander are unchanged.
- FollowsAuthoredMotion: the second hand follows the main hand's rule.
  Its trajectory turns with the facing at its authored key times, and
  its rotation art, depth and timing are kept. It needs no
  SecondaryGripPoint, emits no sorting and leaves the sprite to the
  LeftHand layer.

Validation rejects a second-hand mode on one-handed weapons and only
requires a distinct SecondaryGripPoint for HoldsSecondaryGrip.
LegacyRanged remains for Long Bow and Compound Bow.

Update generator, set, animator and catalog tests, and document the
contract in PlayerCombatArchitecture.md.

commits.subject: feat(vfx): add Cast Flash attack VFX with Magic Wand alignment

tip, with Magic Wand as its first consumer. The presenter and

commits.subject: feat(vfx): align shared Sword Slash with two-handed Zweihander

commits.subject: feat(vfx): share Dagger Thrust alignment with Magic Cinquedea

Magic Cinquedea plays the same Dagger attack clips as Rondel Dagger, so

commits.subject: feat(vfx): align shared Thrust with Rondel Dagger
commits.body:
Add Rondel Dagger as the second consumer of ThrustVfxVisual through its
own AttackVfxDefinition, reusing the same clip, sprites and visual
definition. No runtime code changes.

- Add RondelDaggerThrustAttackVfx: start 0.14s, unmirrored, reach
  offset 0.5, sorting -9 (north) / 21 (south).
- Fit the six poses to Rondel's own baked attack clips, not to Rapier's

- Keep Rapier's phase: the glint lands 60 ms before the stroke and frame
  3 reaches full extension. Rapier's 0.19s start leaves the art behind
  the dagger tip; starts from 0.10s to 0.17s all align.

  sprite, for a 0.875 blade reach.
- Rename RapierThrustPresentationTests to ThrustPresentationTests and
  cover both weapons: shared visual with separate alignments, Rondel
  configuration, presenter playback in six facings, and blade tracing
  for shorter and longer blade variants without asset changes.
- Document the Rondel alignment in PlayerCombatArchitecture.

Known pre-existing failure, not caused by this change:

commits.subject: feat(vfx): add linear thrust attack VFX and Rapier presentation
commits.body:
Refactor AttackVfxVisualDefinition into an abstract base class and introduce SlashVfxVisualDefinition and ThrustVfxVisualDefinition to support distinct attack geometry archetypes (arc vs linear).

- Delegate directional pose resolution to AttackVfxVisualDefinition subclasses so each visual archetype controls its own placement and sizing around its anchor.
- Implement SlashVfxVisualDefinition to scale arc-shaped swings by tip radius.
- Implement ThrustVfxVisualDefinition to scale straight-line thrusts along their local +X path (BackX to FrontX) and shift the origin to the stroke anchor.
- Add Thrust VFX art assets (ThrustVfx.anim, VFX-Thrust.png) and configure ThrustVfxVisual and RapierThrustAttackVfx ScriptableObjects.
- Wire RapierWeaponDefinition presentation with RapierThrustAttackVfx, blade tip, and alignment for all 6 directions starting at 0.19s.
- Update SwordSlashPresentationTests and add RapierThrustPresentationTests to cover geometry validation, pose transformations, animator phase sampling, and presenter playback.
- Document polymorphic Attack VFX geometry and Rapier thrust alignment in PlayerCombatArchitecture.

commits.subject: feat(vfx): align shared Sword Slash with two-handed LongSword
commits.body:

definition. No runtime code changes.

- Fit the six poses (arc center, rotation, reach offset) to the blade
  tip path of LongSword's own baked 2H clips, not to another sword's

  with the widest margin: frame 0 anticipates the windup apex, frames

  SecondaryGripPoint.
- Extend SwordSlashPresentationTests: shared visual across three
  swords, LongSword alignment and 2H contract, rotational sense,
  blade-tip tracing in six facings with geometry variants, independence

  ArmingSword edits.

commits.subject: feat(animation): migrate LongSword to two-handed generic attacks
commits.body:
Extend the directional attack baker with a two-handed contract and move
LongSword off the LegacySword fallback onto the generic Attack route.

Two-handed contract:
- DirectionalAnimationGenerator takes the weapon definition; handedness
  comes from it, never from weapon identity. One-handed output is unchanged.
- Two-handed output keeps the authored LeftHandPivot/LeftHand transform
  (rotation art and key times). OffHandGrip stays empty because the weapon
  blocks the Off Hand, and the LeftHand layer keeps owning the hand sprite.
- The second-hand position is derived from the new
  WeaponDefinition.Presentation.SecondaryGripPoint. The baker carries that
  point along the path the presenter uses for the held weapon (MainHandGrip,
  main-hand rotation, facing with its left mirror, angle correction), then
  subtracts the facing's LeftHand idle sprite anchor, so the drawn hand
  lands on the handle.
- The derived position is keyed at the authored key times plus the clip's
  frame grid, so the hand follows the rotating handle within half a pixel.
- The second hand draws over the handle and under the main hand:
  sorting order 25 in front facings, -5 in north facings.
- WeaponDefinition rejects a two-handed generic attack whose secondary grip
  point equals its grip point.

LongSword:
- LongSword_Attack.anim remains the single south source; six one-shot
  clips are generated under Animations/Weapons/Directional/LongSword.
- New LongSword attack animation set; the definition uses category None.
- Main hand grips the handle row under the guard (0, -0.46875) and the
  second hand the last handle row (0, -0.65625).
- Zweihander keeps the LegacySword fallback.

Tests cover the six directions, determinism and GUID-stable rebakes, the
unchanged authored rotation, second-hand placement on the secondary grip,
sorting, the one-handed contract and the new validation rule.
PlayerCombatArchitecture documents the contract.

commits.subject: fix(vfx): align sword slash with blade trajectory using weapon blade reach
commits.body:
The slash used absolute VisualRoot poses (scale 0.65, rotation 0), so its
tip radius (1.05 * 0.65 = 0.68u) sat well inside the measured blade tip arc
(1.0-1.6u around a center ~0.52u ahead of facing) and was not oriented per
facing. Sizes were also tied to Arming Sword proportions.

Make the alignment data-driven and swing-relative:

- WeaponDefinition.Presentation gains BladeTip, in the weapon sprite's local
  units beside GripPoint. BladeReach is their distance.
- AttackVfxDefinition gains TipRadius (radius the blade tip traces through
  the sprite frames). Directional poses now hold the swing arc center,
  rotation, ReachOffset, Mirrored and sorting instead of an absolute scale.
- TryResolvePose derives the uniform scale as
  (ReachOffset + BladeReach) / TipRadius, negated on Y when mirrored.
- PlayerAttackVfxPresenter only applies the resolved pose; it knows no
  weapon or VFX measurements. The effect stays a direct child of VisualRoot,
  so it never inherits the swing twice.
- Weapon validation requires a blade tip distinct from the grip and a
  positive resolved size for every facing.

Arming Sword poses were fitted from its six directional clips (tip-path
circle fit, mean radial residual ~0.055u). The tip arc center stays stable
across blade reaches 0.8-2.0 (drift <= 0.07u), so weapons sharing the swing
animation can share SwordSlashAttackVfx. The rotational-sense fix is kept:
all poses remain mirrored.

Tests:
- AttackVfx_TracesBladeTipForSwordAndVariantGeometries samples the real
  blade tip with production grip/facing mator
  <= 0.1u) and per-frame angular coverage in all six facings, for Arming
  Sword and short/long geometry variants sharing the same Attack VFX.
- SharedAttackVfx_ResizesFromBladeReachWith
  WeaponWithAttackVfx_RequiresBladeTipDistinctFromGrip cover resolution                                                 and validation.
- Existing pose and configuration tests updated to the new contract.

Docs: PlayerCombatArchitecture.md describes the new Attack VFX contract.

commits.subject: fix(vfx): match sword slash sweep direction to swing in south facings
commits.body:
The canonical VFX-Slash sequence sweeps clockwise around its pivot, while
every ArmingSword directional attack clip rotates the hand counter-clockwise
(shared RightHand z curve: 0 -> -49.2 -> 57.5 -> 69.0; the generator only
rotates hand position per direction). North poses were already mirrored, so
N/NE/NW played in the swing's direction, but S/SE/SW were unmirrored and
played reversed.

- Mirror the S/SE/SW poses in SwordSlashAttackVfx (scale.y 0.65 -> -0.65).
  Position, rotation, sorting and SwordSlashVfx.anim are unchanged.
- Replace the front/back pose-group assertions with a data-driven contract:
  AttackVfx_SweepsInSameRotationalSenseAsWeaponSwing applies each configured
  DirectionalPose through the presenter and compares the signed angular
  sweep of the VFX frame centroids with the main-hand grip sweep during the
  VFX window, both in Animator root space. It covers every catalog weapon
  with an Attack VFX and does not assume a mirror axis or weapon.
- ConfirmedSwordAttack_CapturesConfiguredDirectionalPose now asserts the
  presenter applies the configured pose for each direction.
- Keep a separate configuration test pinning the serialized pose values.

Spatial alignment of the slash with the blade is out of scope and left for
a follow-up.

This change adds frozen duo teammate resolution from the launch roster and projects the teammate's health into the local HUD. It introduces `RaidInitialAffiliationSnapshot.TryGetTeammateProfileId`, binds a new `RaidTeammateHudPresenter`/`RaidTeammateHudView`, and wires it into `LocalPlayerHudBinder`.

commits.subject: Split player spawns into team-based areas
commits.body: Refactors scene spawn configuration to move players out of generic SpawnGroupDefinition into dedicated PlayerSpawnAreaDefinition collections, and marks SpawnGroupType.Players as unsupported in initial world-group dispatch. NetworkSpawnManager now tracks player areas separately, validates them against scene ownership, uses fresh-session-only preflight checks, and resolves player spawn transforms via team/participant assignment rules. RaidParticipantSpawnRules was expanded to validate full fresh launch context, enforce unique transform/position usage, and deterministically map participants to area/point pairs by team appearance and intra-team order. Updated gameplay scene data, architecture docs, and edit-mode tests to cover the new model and reject legacy generic player groups.

commits.subject: Add duo party continuation restoration
commits.body:
Introduce `TownPartyContinuationContext` and an authority-side `TownPartyContinuationClaimRegistry` to preserve and restore solo/duo Town parties after runner replacement. The session coordinator now keeps a pending continuation claim, validates restoration against the recreated Town roster, and supports explicit abandonment.

`TownRaidPreparationDirectory` now coordinates claim/ack/invalidations via RPCs, rebuild-triggered claim epochs, and authority-side restoration spawning when all required members claim. While continuation is pending, ordinary create/join/ready/start requests are blocked, and the presenter/view show a pending-party state with an abandon action.

Town preparation capacity is now explicitly capped at 2 (`TownRaidPreparationRules.MaxMembers`) while keeping raid session max participants unchanged. Related networking/controller logic, tests, and architecture docs were updated to reflect duo-only preparation and continuation claim behavior.

commits.subject: fix: persist prepared equipment changes to backend on equip/unequip
commits.body:
El equipamiento (prepared equipment) se mutaba solo en el estado local
al equipar/desequipar desde el stash, a diferencia de las transferencias
stash<->loadout que sí sincronizan con el backend. Como resultado, el
equipo sobrevivía dentro de una misma sesión de juego pero se perdía
tras logout/login, porque nunca llegaba a persistirse vía
PUT /character/me/inventory/prepared-equipment.

OnPreparedEquipmentAssignmentRequested y OnPreparedEquipmentClearRequested
ahora, tras la mutación local exitosa, sincronizan el estado resultante
al backend a través de RemoteInventoryService.UpdatePreparedEquipmentAsync
(endpoint ya existente pero nunca invocado).

commits.subject: Add authoritative extraction commit flow
commits.body: Adds an authoritative extraction result model and backend flow for raid commits. The service now prefers Fusion-backed extraction data, applies progression and loot atomically with idempotent safeguards, and preserves prepared equipment/progression receipts while reusing the character update path. commits.subject: Add runtime attribute override flow for raids
commits.body:
Introduces a development-only runtime attribute override system that composes session offsets over persistent raid attributes without touching profile persistence. Adds `RuntimeAttributeOverrideState/Session`, a replicated `RuntimeAttributeOverrideNetworkController`, and a local developer IMGUI panel in Town/Raid prefabs.

`NetworkRaidParticipant` now exposes effective attributes (plus persistent read and revision), and consumers were updated to react to override revisions: weapon equipment revalidates requirements/scaling, player max health caches by revision, and health is clamped after max-health decreases. Includes prefab wiring, edit/play mode coverage for override behavior, and architecture docs updates to reflect the effective-attribute model.

commits.subject: fix(presentation): reserve sorting slots for equipment layers
commits.body:
The modular character rendered each equipment layer at base+1, but the
base body parts used consecutive sorting orders (Legs=1, Body=2,
LeftHand=3, Head=4), leaving no gap. Every equipment layer therefore
landed on the next base part: Boots tied Body, Armor tied LeftHand and
LeftGlove tied Head. Equal sortingOrder makes the draw order
non-deterministic, most visibly the Boots (leg armor) clipping against
the Body.

Re-space the base parts so each reserves a free slot above it while
keeping their relative order identical (Legs=0, Body=2, LeftHand=4,
Head=6; Body and RightHand=30 left untouched to preserve the weapon
relationship). Equipment now lands in the gaps with no ties:
Legs<Boots<Body<Armor<LeftHand<LeftGlove<Head<Helmet.

Extract the base+offset into EquipmentLayerSortingRule so the layer
tracking stays dynamic and per-slot (no per-set hardcoding), and add
EditMode tests: offset preserved as base order changes, base parts have
distinct orders, no equipment layer collides with a foreign base part,
and the intended back-to-front stack is preserved.

commits.subject: fix(combat): aim ranged enemy attacks at the target's current position
commits.body:
fix(combat): aim ranged enemy attacks at the target's current position

Ranged enemies fired every projectile toward a stale direction once the
player entered attack range.

Two defects compounded:

- EnemyMovementAIController gated the FacingDirection write behind
  canMove. EnemyAttackState disables control to hold the enemy still,
  so facing stopped updating entirely on entering Attack.
- EnemyCombatAIController passed that frozen FacingDirection into
  TryCommitAttack. FacingDirection derives from the pursuit path and can
  point around an obstacle, so it is not a valid aim source even when it
  does update.

Facing now resolves toward the target's current position while movement
is disabled, keeping the enemy stationary but tracking. Ranged aim is
computed per attack from _attackOrigin to the target. Melee keeps
consuming FacingDirection, so its arc is unchanged. The direction is
frozen into the pending AttackRequest at commit time, so a projectile
keeps the direction it was fired with and never homes.

Reuses the existing PlayerAimMath.TryResolveDirection helper instead of
adding new direction math. Documents the facing/aim boundary in
EnemyCombatArchitecture.md.

fix(networking): return the Host to Town after Cancel Raid
commits.body:
Cancel Raid aborted every participant with return authorization, including the
operational Host's. RaidMenuPresenter observed IsReturnAuthorized without
distinguishing roles and called ReturnParticipantToTownAsync(), which
SessionConnectionCoordinator correctly rejects for an operational Host with
InvalidRequest, leaving the return latch set, the menu closed and the Host stuck
in Gameplay with a live runner.

A cancelled Host participant ends as Aborted with FinalizationCause.None, so it is
not an accepted terminal result and RaidResultsReturnPolicy cannot authorize its
Results return. That gate stays unchanged; the cancellation return gets its own
explicit entry point into the existing pending-Host-return lifecycle.

- RaidMenuPresenter: gate the individual participant return behind
  ShouldStartParticipantReturn, which requires a resolved non-Host operational
  role, so an unresolved role during shutdown starts nothing. The operational Host
  only acknowledges the closure locally, once, when its participant is authorized.
- RaidMenuPresenter: inspect the SessionTransitionResult of the participant return
  and release the latch, restoring the menu, on any non-Succeeded result instead of
  leaving the UI silently closed. Exceptions remain a separate failure path.
- SessionConnectionCoordinator: arm the existing pending host-return latch once when
  an authoritative HostCancellation closure is observed. ObservePendingHostResultsReturn
  still starts the single global ReturnToTownAsync() only at MatchPhase.Finished with
  no Raiding participants and no connected remote peers, so the Host keeps the
  authoritative runner while Clients remain.
- Document the two valid entry points of the pending operational-Host return in
  LobbyAndSessionTransitionArchitecture.md.

Clients keep their existing individual participant return. Host Migration is
unaffected: only RaidClosureReason.HostCancellation arms this path.

EditMode: 961/978 passed; the 17 failures are pre-existing prefab, animation and
loot asset checks unrelated to this change. The touched fixtures pass 113/113.
Solo-Host and two-application Host+Client cancellation still require manual Unity
validation.

commits.subject: Unify the Stash screen with the Raid inventory and prepare Equipment in Town
commits.body:
The Stash screen was a fork of the Raid inventory that stopped matching it when
the Raid UI moved into the prefab: it still instantiated slots at runtime, kept
two dead RaidLootPanelView components wired to a removed _slotPrefab field, and
floated its two prepared weapon slots over the loadout panel with hardcoded
anchored positions. Town preparation also covered weapons only, so the armor
introduced by the six-slot Equipment work could not be prepared before a raid.

Stash screen composition
- LobbyStashUI stops creating UI. It binds two authored RaidLootPanelView panels,
  six authored RaidInventorySlotView Equipment views, both bulk buttons and the
  context menu, and pads each received stack list with empty entries up to its
  authored pool exactly as RaidInventoryProjection does for the Raid screen.
  Content beyond the pool is reported once and the panel shows its existing
  "Lleno" feedback instead of silently dropping stacks.
- Both panels are TransferWithContextMenu, so a stack can be equipped from the
  Stash or from the Loadout. The menu offers only the slots EquipmentSlotRules
  reports as compatible, resolved from the category now carried by
  RaidInventorySlotData, so the view needs no catalog of its own. A left click on
  an occupied Equipment slot releases that exact slot.
- TownStashView becomes an authored component that only shows and hides the
  screen; TownStashPresenter resolves it instead of adding components and the
  Canvas sorting order is authored in the prefab. The development-only [StashUI]
  traces are gone; the dependency warnings stay.
- StashInventory.prefab now holds the panels, both 16-slot pools, the equipment
  panel and the screen root. The prefab is the only source of truth for that
  layout: the temporary authoring tools that seeded both inventory screens are
  removed, so nothing can regenerate the hierarchy, renumber the authored slots
  or overwrite manual layout work. Adding a slot means adding it in the prefab
  and appending it to the panel's _authoredSlots.

Town Equipment preparation
- PreparedWeaponLoadout becomes PreparedEquipmentLoadout, covering the six slots
  of EquipmentSlot. EquipmentSlotRules owns the canonical slot order and decides
  compatibility; weapon slots additionally require a usable WeaponDefinition, and
  one identity used by several slots requires one owned unit per reference.
- LocalProfileStore exposes TryAssignPreparedEquipment/TryClearPreparedEquipment.
  Prepared units must belong to the Loadout because that is what the reservation
  transfers, so equipping a unit that still lives in the Stash pulls the missing
  units into the Loadout inside the same atomic commit; a rejected assignment
  moves nothing and a full Loadout rejects the pull. Releasing a slot leaves the
  unit in the Loadout. Reconciliation releases the last slots first.
- The recovery weapon guarantee and the Slot 2 to Slot 1 normalization no longer
  overwrite prepared armor: armor is optional, never granted and never rewritten.
- The profile codec gains four additive armor fields for the profile and for the
  reservation. CurrentSchemaVersion stays 1 on purpose: the fields are optional,
  so a profile saved before them decodes with empty armor, while bumping the
  version would reject every existing local profile as UnsupportedVersion.
- RaidAdmissionData carries one reference per Equipment slot in
  EquipmentSlotRules.AllSlots order, RaidLoadoutRules validates range, the
  mandatory weapon and reference multiplicity, and the admission token moves to
  canonical version 6 with four extra bytes, still inside its 512-byte bound.
- TryInitializePreparedEquipment equips the six slots on spawn and rechecks slot
  compatibility against the catalog before extracting any unit, so a reference
  that no longer fits its slot rejects the admission instead of dropping the
  piece. FusionSessionLauncher verifies all six slots before confirming.

Design alignment
04 - Character Build Design puts armor inside the prepared build and allows
changing it in Town, and keeps one valid weapon as the only launch requirement.
02 - Estados del Juego enables Inventory, Equipment and Stash during Expedition
Preparation. Armor still carries no stats, as documented in PlayerCombat.

Verification
- Assembly-CSharp and Assembly-CSharp-Editor compile with 0 errors; the remaining
  warnings are pre-existing.
- The full EditMode suite was run after the Stash unification only: 706/720, with
  the same 14 pre-existing failures as the previous commit. It has NOT been run
  again after the Equipment preparation change, which updates existing tests and
  adds PreparedEquipmentTests.
- Manual: the Stash screen was opened in the Editor after authoring and presents
  the six Equipment slots and both panels correctly. A complete Town to Raid cycle
  carrying prepared armor, and Host/Client admission, remain manually unverified.

commits.subject: Add six-slot player Equipment and move raid inventory UI into the prefab
commits.body:
Equipment stops being "the weapon system" and becomes the single authoritative
source of what the player has equipped, covering the six MVP slots defined by
Character Build: two weapon quick slots plus Helmet, Armor, Gloves and Boots.

Slot contracts (Assets/Scripts/Player/Equipment/)
- EquipmentSlot enumerates exactly the six slots; the two weapon values match
  WeaponSlot so the value already replicated by the active-weapon selection and
  carried by the equipment RPC keeps its meaning.
- EquipmentSlotRules is the single source of truth for compatibility. Loot only
  classifies a unit through LootCategory (extended with Helmet/Armor/Gloves/
  Boots, preserving existing serialized values); deciding which slot may receive
  it belongs to Equipment. No ArmorDefinition and no armor stats were added.
- WeaponEquipResult becomes EquipmentOperationResult with explicit numeric
  values, since results travel through the RPC as ints. Value 5 stays reserved
  by the removed WeaponAlreadyEquipped result. Armor operations no longer report
  weapon-flavoured errors.

Authoritative state
- PlayerWeaponEquipmentNetworkController is evolved rather than rewritten or
  renamed. Four networked catalog-index properties join the existing weapon
  slots; the replicated shape is otherwise untouched, so Host Migration keeps
  restoring through the same [Networked] mechanism with no new logic.
- Dependency validation is split: every equip/unequip needs only catalog,
  receiver and character, while the combat strategies are validated solely on
  the weapon branch. Equipping a helmet no longer depends on the projectile
  spawner.
- Armor never calls TryConfigureStrategy, TrySetActiveAttack or
  TryClearActiveAttack, and never enters the weapon-state comparison (renamed
  HasReplicatedWeaponStateChanged), so it cannot rebuild the active attack or
  disturb the authoritative cooldown. EquipmentRevision advances for all six
  slots. Rejected operations mutate neither Inventory nor Equipment.

Expedition ownership
- PlayerExpeditionLootSnapshot captures the six slots as named properties, not a
  positional array, and aggregates them into Combined. Equipped armor is now
  expedition property: lost on defeat and kept on extraction like a weapon.

Raid inventory UI
- No player UI component is created at runtime any more. RaidInventoryView
  exposes one named serialized field per equipment slot and RaidLootPanelView
  drives a serialized slot pool, showing the first N and hiding the rest instead
  of instantiating and destroying views.
- The Editor tool Grimhold/UI/Rebuild Raid Inventory UI authors the equipment
  panel and the three slot pools into NetworkPlayer.prefab through PrefabUtility,
  so the hierarchy stays fully editable in the Inspector.

Placeholder content
- Four placeholder armor definitions reuse the existing character body-part
  sprites so every slot can be exercised before real art exists. They are sold
  by the merchant and present in the container loot table. Town armor
  preparation is not implemented by this task; PreparedWeaponLoadout stays
  weapon-only.

Verification
- EditMode 706/720; the 14 failures are pre-existing (missing enemy prefabs and
  slime clip, SocialPlayer composition, Coins/Bone sell values).
- The 51 new EditMode equipment tests and the 9 new PlayMode tests all pass.
- PlayMode compared against a clean HEAD baseline: 84 failures before, 83 after,
  with no new failures introduced.

commits.subject: Complete two-slot weapon equipment and expedition preparation
commits.body:
Extend Weapon Equipment to two authoritative quick slots and carry them across the
Town-Raid boundary. Prepared Weapon Slot 1 and Slot 2 are non-owning references over units
that remain in the Town Loadout; they enter the raid inside PendingLoadoutReservation, travel
as compact one-based references into ReservedLoadout in the version 5 admission token, and are
materialized by State Authority into replicated Equipment without duplicating inventory
ownership. Add the Town assignment UI over the Loadout context menu, raid inventory weapon
slots, weapon selection input, and the corresponding persistence, codec and admission coverage.

Introduce an expedition preparation boundary that runs before the reservation so requiring a
valid equipped weapon can no longer make Start Raid inert. TryPrepareExpeditionWeapons is
atomic, deterministic and idempotent: it leaves a valid Slot 1 untouched, normalizes the
effective selection when only Slot 2 is occupied, grants exactly one configured recovery weapon
when nothing is prepared while reusing an owned unit first, and fails explicitly on a persisted
reference that no longer resolves instead of overwriting it. Add the recovery_sword definition
with its own weapon definition, excluded from loot tables and without economic value, and
configure it as the Town recovery policy. TryCreateLoadoutReservation keeps requiring a valid
prepared weapon as a domain invariant, and Raid never grants recovery.

Stop a rejected local preparation from deadlocking the shared Town preparation.
TryStoreRaidLaunchContext now returns RaidLaunchPreparationResult so a transient retry is
distinguishable from a permanent rejection; a peer that cannot prepare reports it once per
launch revision instead of sending a false acknowledgement or waiting silently, and the State
Authority remains the only canceller. Arm a deadline for the acknowledgement phase so a launch
revision cannot wait indefinitely for a missing acknowledgement, and surface the rejection
reason through the existing Town feedback channel.

Fix two crashes in the new equipment surface. Every read-only query is guarded behind the
spawn check so presentation components that run their lifecycle callbacks during prefab
instantiation report no equipment rather than throwing on networked state, and the equipment
request RPC validates its byte-backed kind by range because Enum.IsDefined rejects the boxed
int outright.

commits.subject: implement core game feel systems (screen shake, knockback, reactive aggro)
commits.body:
Introduces three major game feel and feedback mechanics into the combat system to improve impact satisfaction and AI responsiveness:

1. Camera Screen Shake
- Implemented a trauma-based perlin noise camera shake system.
- Triggered on the local client via `LocalPlayerCameraShakeBinder` when receiving damage or confirming a valid hit against an enemy. Breakables are excluded.
- Controlled via `CameraShakeConfig` asset.

2. Physics-respecting Knockback
- Added configurable `KnockbackForce` to all `AttackConfig` assets.
- Both players and enemies receive an instantaneous impulse (`KnockbackVelocity`) that gracefully decays over time via friction.
- The displacement is fully resolved against world geometry by the `Kinematic2DMovementMotor`.

3. Reactive Targeting (Aggro)
- Enemies now instantly acquire the player as a target when hit by an attack, even from outside their normal line of sight or disengage range.
- Bypasses standard LOS checks for a configurable duration (`_aggroAlertDuration`) to ensure the enemy actively pursues the attacker.

Architecture:
- Added `IKnockbackMotor` and `IKnockbackReceiver` for universal knockback application without coupling DamageResolver to movement implementations.
- Added `IAggroReceiver` to `EnemyMovementAIController` to handle alert states.
- Extended `EntityRegistry` to safely resolve transforms, player identity, and feedback sinks during damage resolution.

Implements Stage 3 of US-16.

Introduces a robust idempotency protocol to handle network retries without double-execution:
- Created MerchantRequestValidator running on the Master Client to deduplicate incoming RPCs by maintaining a log of (PlayerRef, sequence) -> ShopTransactionId.
- Created MerchantTransactionOrchestrator on the requesting client to assign sequences, drop duplicate network responses, resolve prices locally against the LootDefinitionCatalog, and enforce atomic writes via LocalProfileStore.
- Decoupled interactable endpoints (TownMerchantNpcInteractable) from network logic (TownMerchantNetworkController).
- Removed declaredPrice from network payloads completely, cementing a Client-trusted / Local-authoritative economy model.
- Added 14 EditMode tests covering protocol collisions, replay scenarios, and lost responses.

commits.subject: add late-join prevention and scene spawn-point policy architecture
commits.body:
- Enforced authoritative coordinator persistence by spawning the NetworkMatchController with Photon Fusion's managed `NetworkSpawnFlags.DontDestroyOnLoad` flags.
- Replaced global ActiveScene fallbacks with runner-scoped scene resolution using `runner.SceneManager.MainRunnerScene` exclusively.
- Implemented a declarative scene configuration system (`SceneSpawnPointPolicy`) to explicitly declare whether a scene requires spawn points (`Required`) or not (`NotRequired`).
- Decoupled spatial scene configuration into `NetworkSpawnSceneConfiguration` and spawn group definitions (`SpawnGroupType`, `SpawnGroupDefinition`).
- Enforced a fail-closed spawning pipeline using incremental load generations and tracking states (Pending, Processing, Completed, Failed) to deduplicate callback execution.
- Added strict validations: `CanUseCurrentSceneSpawnPoints` for spatial-based entities and `CanSpawnAtExplicitTransform` for explicit coordinate-based spawns.
- Fixed an enemy spawning bug by refactoring `_spawnedEnemies` from a dictionary to a list to prevent duplicate key exceptions.
- Added visual/console feedback message when a client fails or is rejected to join an already started session.
- Updated launcher start/shutdown lifecycles with secure try-finally blocks and async cleanup.
- Refactored all networking code and architecture documents to align with the new spawn-point terminology.

evidence.value: add late-join prevention and scene spawn-point policy architecture
